## Maintainer clarification: full language support and CSTs by default are required The maintainer has clarified the acceptance scope: > There should be no limitations. Meta language must fully support representation and transformation of all the requested languages, and all the existing languages as CST by default. Treat this as a required correction to PR #196's intermediate scope. Full support for JavaScript, Rust, Rocq/Coq and Lean remains required, and **full concrete syntax trees must be the default representation for all existing languages**. The current four-language lexical subset, unavailable capability reports and unsupported translation descriptors do not fulfill that request. Complete the implementation in this PR; do not resolve the requirement by documenting the missing features as permanent exclusions. ### 1. Default CST support must cover the complete language inventory - [ ] Build one authoritative, versioned language/grammar inventory shared by both runtime packages. Reconcile it with every parser dispatch, alias, extension, advertised language, dialect, grammar importer, embedded-language target and conformance fixture. The current inventory is a minimum coverage audit, not permission to limit the maintainer's “all existing languages” requirement to four languages or a frozen shortlist. - [ ] For every language, the ordinary parse API must select its real grammar and construct a complete, lossless CST as links by default. Preserve grammatical node kinds, named fields, child order, all tokens/trivia/comments, exact source spans, error and missing nodes, and embedded-language boundaries. A root node around characters or delimiter groups is not a complete CST. - [ ] Supply default grammars and extension infrastructure that can express the full language syntax, including context-sensitive/project-defined notation, macros, dialects and embedded regions. Where parsing needs a project, imports or syntax extensions, accept and resolve that context rather than permanently declaring the construct opaque. Preserve surface syntax alongside expansion/elaboration and trace their relationship. - [ ] Provide equivalent default capabilities in JavaScript and Rust. Reuse mature grammars and common parser implementations/artifacts where practical. Lowering the advertised parity contract to the weaker scanner does not satisfy the full-CST requirement. - [ ] Keep missing grammars or unimplemented constructs visibly incomplete until implemented. A generic byte/text representation is useful storage, but must not satisfy a language's CST coverage gate. Do not remove a language, alias or construct from the inventory to make CI green. At head `c1ec894bff736677537810d701111c06069d003a`, the [Rust dispatcher](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/c1ec894bff736677537810d701111c06069d003a/rust/src/tree_sitter_adapter.rs#L141) already names Python, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Visual Basic, Delphi/Object Pascal, Rust, Go, R, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Perl, eight SQL dialect profiles, HTML, CSS, JSON, YAML, TOML, XML/DTD, INI, Protocol Buffers and GraphQL. Other paths add Lean/Rocq, LiNo, CSV, JSON5, markup and embedded regions. Audit the [target registries](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/c1ec894bff736677537810d701111c06069d003a/rust/src/parity.rs#L572), natural-language and document representations too; retain their own meaningful syntax structures and do not silently drop them from the broader inventory. I reproduced the default-path gap in the PR's JavaScript package: | Input language | Example | Syntax links returned | |---|---|---:| | Python | `def f(x):\n return x + 1\n` | 0 | | TypeScript | `const x: number = 1;` | 0 | | Java | `class Main {}` | 0 | | Go | `package main\nfunc main() {}` | 0 | | JSON | `{"x":1}` | 0 | | HTML | `

Hello

` | 0 | All six inputs round-trip as text. That confirms preservation but does not establish the CST support requested here. ### 2. Full representation and transformation for the four requested languages - [ ] Cover the entire syntax and structured representation of JavaScript, Rust, Rocq and Lean, including imports/modules, scopes/bindings, recursive definitions, types/universes, effects, attributes, macros/notation, proof terms and tactics. Track grammar/version/edition coverage with executable evidence. A version string in a capability object is not proof of conformance to that language version. - [ ] Provide structure-aware query, insert, delete, replace, move, clone and construction of syntax; support generation from newly constructed or transformed networks, without relying on an untouched original source buffer. Update structure, spans, source mappings and diagnostics after edits, and verify emitted code reparses into the intended structure. - [ ] Implement binding-aware rename and transformations that preserve the intended meaning, including nested scopes, shadowing, capture avoidance, qualified/module names, macros and proof binders. Syntax-only transformations must identify their scope; do not label spelling substitution as semantic refactoring. - [ ] Keep genuinely shared language concepts reusable in meta-language and preserve language-specific distinctions and context explicitly. RML-specific syntax, foundations and proof authority remain in RML; their representation must use the full upstream infrastructure. - [ ] Preserve the existing requirement for all 12 directed translations among the four languages, with actual implementations, faithful encodings/runtime support where necessary, source mappings and behavioral/type/proof-preservation evidence. `UnsupportedObligation` is an honest report of unfinished work, not a completed translation implementation. CST availability alone does not complete translation. The lexical implementation still fails ordinary JavaScript cases. I ran these against this PR, in addition to the original fixed string/comment regression: ```text Rename identifier x -> y: input: const x = 1; const re = /x/; x; actual: const y = 1; const re = /y/; y; error: the regular-expression literal was changed as though it were an identifier. input: const x = 1; const text = `value: ${x}`; actual: const y = 1; const text = `value: ${x}`; error: the expression reference inside the template literal was not changed. parse: const = ; actual: verifyFullMatch().isClean() === true error: a clean lexical scan is being exposed without a full grammatical validity check. ``` Correct these failures and add them to the shared regression corpus. Cover the equivalent language-specific cases, not only these strings. Error recovery should preserve invalid source and report grammar errors rather than presenting it as a valid program. ### 3. Evidence, release delivery and completion - [ ] Commit an atomic requirement/coverage ledger preserving issue #195 and this clarification. Map every language and construct to grammar, implementation, positive/negative tests and transformation evidence in both runtimes. Do not replace missing implementation with more declarations, capability enums or documentation. - [ ] Use upstream language conformance suites, grammar corpora and representative real projects in addition to small fixtures. Exercise malformed input, comments/literals/interpolation, Unicode, macros, modules, proof syntax, mixed-language files and sequences of edits. Verify real node kinds/fields and tree relationships; a root node and an exact text round trip are insufficient. - [ ] Test both runtimes against the same expected CST/semantic contracts. Where internal layouts differ, normalize them under an explicit faithful mapping; do not erase distinctions merely to pass parity. Test against native parsers/compilers/provers where relevant, keeping those checks distinct from RML's internal reasoning authority. - [ ] Install and test the actually published npm and Rust artifacts. Resolve the continuing npm distribution gap linked in [#171](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/171), and demonstrate downstream RML integration with the released capabilities. - [ ] Update the PR description and docs to preserve **full support as the delivery requirement**. Report current gaps honestly during development. The present 97 passing JS tests and green CI do not discharge missing grammar, semantic transformation or translation coverage. - [ ] Remove the trailing `Fixes #195` while required work remains incomplete. The body currently says the issue must remain open and then supplies a directive that would close it on merge. Do not close #195 or claim completion until the full requirements are implemented and verified; a documented “intermediate foundation” is not the requested final result. This clarification changes the acceptance target; it does not authorize claiming that the current implementation already has no limitations. Implement the missing capabilities, keep failures observable while doing so, and supply the evidence before marking the work complete.

issue.title: Full four-language representation and transformation; default CST support for all languages
issue.body:
## Maintainer clarification — full support is required (2026-09-23)

> There should be no limitations. Meta language must fully support representation and transformation of all the requested languages, and all the existing languages as CST by default.

The required result is **full representation and transformation of JavaScript, Rust, Rocq/Coq and Lean, plus complete lossless CSTs by default for all existing languages**, with equivalent capabilities in JavaScript and Rust. The current repository language inventory is a minimum coverage audit, not a cap on this requirement.

The [detailed acceptance clarification and reproduced gaps on PR #196](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5795832509) is part of this issue's requirements and must be added to the committed requirement ledger.

- [ ] Deliver grammar-level CSTs through the normal parse API for every language, including existing dialects, aliases and embedded-language paths. Generic text, token streams and delimiter groups do not satisfy CST support.
- [ ] Deliver complete structured representation and transformation for the four requested languages, including bindings/scopes, project context, modules, types, macros/notation and proof/tactic syntax; support structured construction, edits and source generation.
- [ ] Implement the 12 directed cross-language translations already requested, with explicit preservation contracts and tested faithful encodings. Unsupported descriptors are unfinished work, not completed translations.
- [ ] Verify all capabilities using shared JS/Rust grammar and transformation corpora, real projects, negative cases and actual published packages. Do not lower parity to the weaker implementation or remove languages/constructs to pass coverage.
- [ ] Complete the implementation in PR #196, retain every earlier requirement below, and keep this issue open until delivery evidence exists. Do not treat a documented intermediate subset as completion.

This clarification supersedes any interpretation of the original wording that permits permanent omissions or unsupported/opaque capability reports to count as delivered full support. During implementation, diagnostics and status reports must remain truthful; marking a limitation as documented does not resolve it.

## Original request and evidence

RML needs complete, editable representations of JavaScript, Rust, Rocq, and Lean supplied by `meta-language`, with the same observable contracts in its JavaScript and Rust packages. This is an upstream dependency request from the review of [relative-meta-logic PR #184](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic/pull/184), following the maintainer's [four-language requirement](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic/pull/184#issuecomment-5773514118).

The requested result is structured language representation and translation infrastructure. RML will own its logic, proof checking, execution semantics, selectable foundations, and RML-specific language extension. Generic concepts shared by languages should live here when their meanings actually coincide.

## Verified gaps, 2026-09-23

Reviewed meta-language main at `922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664` (source version 0.58.2), and RML PR head `c24f5b98cc2f6bce2145993d7a1a6b03f2e67122`.

1. [`js/src/network.js:27`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664/js/src/network.js#L27) handles `lino` specially and routes other languages through `parseLosslessText`. `_indexJavaScriptIdentifiers` uses a regular expression, not a JavaScript parser. Rust/Lean/Rocq inputs produce source-token links without language syntax structure. Text preservation alone does not establish language support.
2. [`rust/src/tree_sitter_adapter.rs:141`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664/rust/src/tree_sitter_adapter.rs#L141) has JavaScript and Rust grammar dispatch, but no Lean/Rocq/Coq dispatch. The [built-in parser](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664/rust/src/language_parser.rs) silently falls back to lossless text for those languages. Thus the two runtimes also provide different syntax capabilities.
3. [`parity/language-features.json`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/922474141265251d5295f8882252128da45df664/parity/language-features.json) explicitly exempts the Rust language-parser modules from JavaScript parity. Passing the present parity manifest therefore does not establish four-language parser parity.
4. npm still reports only `meta-language@0.46.0` (`npm view meta-language dist-tags versions --json`), while source and the [latest release](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/releases/tag/v0.58.2) are 0.58.2. RML consequently consumes npm 0.46.0 and Rust 0.58.2. This reproduces the release-distribution concern of closed [#171](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/171); a fix present only in main is not available out of the box to downstream users.

I ran the following on current meta-language source after `cd js && npm ci --ignore-scripts`:

```js
import { LinkNetwork, LinkQuery, ReplacementRule } from './src/index.js';

const source = 'const x = 1; const s = "x"; // x\n';
const network = LinkNetwork.parse(source, 'JavaScript');
const query = LinkQuery.fromSexpression('(identifier) @target\n(#eq? @target "x")');
const matches = network.find(query);
network.replace(matches, ReplacementRule.capturedText('target', 'y'));
console.log(matches.length, network.reconstructText());
```

Actual: three matches and `const y = 1; const s = "y"; // y`. Expected for an identifier-only query: one match, with the string literal and comment preserved. The same failure occurs through RML's published-dependency adapter.

Other current JS-source probes all reconstruct their input exactly, but `fn id(x: u64) -> u64 { x }`, `def id (x : Nat) : Nat := x`, and `Definition id (x : nat) : nat := x.` have only `SourceToken` links. `const x = 1;` has 12 source-token links and one regex-created `Syntax` identifier link, not a full JavaScript syntax tree.

## Acceptance requirements

- [ ] Ship registered parsers and emitters for JavaScript, Rust, Rocq (including the Coq alias), and Lean in both runtime packages. Declare exact supported language versions/editions and extensions, and inventory every language construct against implementation and conformance evidence. Retain the full-coverage requirement; a supported subset is an intermediate state, not completion.
- [ ] Preserve complete source bytes/trivia, syntax hierarchy, identifiers and scope/binding, module/import references, declarations, types/universes, recursive bodies, attributes/macros/notation, effects, and proof/tactic syntax where applicable. Distinguish parsed, resolved, elaborated, and opaque representations. Unknown syntax and unavailable plugins must be reported explicitly, with their source retained; fallback text must never be labelled successful semantic parsing.
- [ ] Provide language-independent links for genuinely shared concepts, with lossless language-specific extensions for differing meanings. Do not equate similar spellings, collapse proof universes, invent compatible effects, or discard unsupported information.
- [ ] Support structured edits and source generation after the original source buffer is unavailable. Add binding-aware rename/capture tests, including identifiers in strings/comments, shadowing, Unicode, nested scopes, macros/notation and invalid input.
- [ ] Expose a stable parse → network → transform → emit contract, fidelity/capability reports, provenance/source mappings, schema versioning and extension registration. Keep RML-specific syntax and proof/foundation policy in RML; make only reusable binding, typing, module, proof-syntax and translation concepts shared here.
- [ ] Supply the common representation and translation hooks needed for all 12 directed pairs among the four languages. Define each translation's observation/semantic-preservation contract, required runtime/encoding and assumptions. Preserve non-native constructs through an explicit supported encoding or return a precise unsupported obligation. Passing text through under a new language label, translating a keyword, or silently weakening a theorem does not count as a translation.
- [ ] Keep source preservation, syntax coverage, semantic lowering, emitted-code validity and behavior/proof preservation as separately tested capabilities. Native compilers/provers may validate emitted artifacts; their success alone does not prove the translation correct or supply RML's internal reasoning authority.
- [ ] Run one shared conformance corpus through both runtime packages, checking normalized links, scopes, diagnostics, reconstruction, mutations and translation results. Remove capability exemptions that conceal these parser gaps. Include corpus-derived negative cases and integration tests consumed by RML.
- [ ] Publish matching usable npm/crates releases and demonstrate installation and the four-language examples from those published artifacts. Resolve or explicitly link the continuing #171 publication problem rather than requiring downstream consumers to pin an unpublished npm version.

Existing closed work on parser registries ([#52](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/52)), shared concepts ([#57](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/57)), translation registries ([#58](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/58)), recursive translation ([#183](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/183)), and grammar translation ([#112](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/112)) provides infrastructure to reuse. It does not demonstrate these four complete language implementations or their cross-language fidelity.

Please keep this request open until the coverage and published-package evidence exists. RML's downstream audit should link the implementing PRs, release versions and integration tests; opening this issue itself is not completion of downstream language support.

## Required acceptance gate: executable verification of every requirement, with no coverage exemptions

The maintainer requests full verification of **all** requirements in tests, so missing implementation cannot be bypassed by a green but incomplete suite. This comment supplements, and does not narrow, [issue #195](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/195), the [full-support clarification](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5795832509), and the committed requirement ledger. Complete the requested implementation in this PR; an intermediate subset or a promise of follow-up work is not acceptance.

### Verified baseline — not completion

At `dc7d6252c418c06db8364b0b483d7c9f26cc2857`, I independently reran `npm test` (102/102 passing) and `npm run check:parity`. The regex, template-interpolation, invalid-syntax, and zero-width-missing-node regressions pass. That progress is real.

However:

- The [inventory/ledger](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/dc7d6252c418c06db8364b0b483d7c9f26cc2857/docs/issue-195-requirement-ledger.md) reports only 43/57 grammar-backed targets in JavaScript and 39/57 in Rust, with other required paths still specialized, lexical, or text-only. These counts include formats and profiles; they are not proof of full language conformance.
- The [inventory test](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/dc7d6252c418c06db8364b0b483d7c9f26cc2857/js/tests/four-language-conformance.test.js) filters to rows already marked `grammar-cst`. Consequently, a missing grammar can remain outside that positive test while CI passes. Test the entire required inventory, not only its implemented subset.
- The same test file explicitly expects unavailable binding/type resolution and expects all 12 translation contracts to be unsupported. Such tests can verify truthful diagnostics, but **cannot count as positive acceptance tests for the requested capabilities**.
- The [implementation](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/dc7d6252c418c06db8364b0b483d7c9f26cc2857/js/src/language-support.js#L85) still declares unavailable resolution/elaboration and no registered translation encodings.
- GitHub currently reports `isDraft: false`, while the description/ledger say draft. The description still ends with `Fixes #195` despite saying the issue will remain open.

### 1. Make requirement traceability machine-checked

- [ ] Commit a machine-readable manifest of **atomic, stable requirement IDs**, preserving every requirement from the issue, its clarification, this comment, and the ledger. Include source permalink, language/version/edition/construct, runtime, implementation entry point, test IDs/fixtures, expected observable behavior, verification checkpoint, and evidence artifact. Split compound requirements so a passing parser test cannot conceal a missing semantic or transformation requirement.
- [ ] Reconcile this manifest automatically with every parser/target registry, advertised language, alias, extension, dialect, grammar importer, embedded-language path, and documentation claim. Fail on missing, duplicate, dangling, or untested entries. The 57-target inventory is a minimum audit, **not a cap on “all existing languages.”** Do not reduce scope by deleting or reclassifying targets or assertions.
- [ ] Generate the human-readable ledger and completion summary from the actual test results and manifest. Hand-edited `Complete` labels, capability enums, test filenames, or self-reported `grammar-cst` statuses are not execution evidence.
- [ ] Every applicable requirement must have positive behavioral coverage in **both JavaScript and Rust**, plus appropriate negative/recovery coverage. A claimed non-applicability needs an explicit technical rationale and maintainer acceptance; missing implementation is not non-applicability.

### 2. Add a mandatory full-requirements CI gate

- [ ] Add a dedicated aggregate acceptance check, running on the exact PR head/merge candidate and included in required merge checks. If configuring repository protection needs maintainer permission, report that explicitly; do not claim the gate is enforced until it is configured.
- [ ] The gate must fail for any required row at its checkpoint that is missing, open, partial, unsupported, unexecuted, skipped, TODO, marked `xfail`, filtered out, or represented only by a placeholder test. Proper negative tests asserting expected diagnostics are required; `xfail` execution of a missing positive capability is not acceptance. Keep diagnostic tests for unfinished paths, but do not let them satisfy delivery tests.
- [ ] All implementation and candidate-artifact verification belongs to the required pre-merge checkpoint. Only checks that inherently require a published release may have a separate mandatory release-delivery checkpoint. Keep those rows visibly pending and overall delivery incomplete until they pass; do not use staging to postpone any language, semantic, transformation, translation, or integration implementation. The release checkpoint must prevent declaring completion/closing the issue on publication or verification failure.
- [ ] No `continue-on-error`, swallowed assertion failures, empty test selection, missing compiler treated as success, optional/manual-only acceptance jobs, capability-based filtering, or parity exemptions for required behavior. Shards are acceptable only if the aggregate verifies the complete expected set actually executed. A cancelled or missing job is not a pass.
- [ ] Test discovery and result ingestion must validate stable test IDs, fixture/corpus identity, and nonzero expected coverage for every matrix cell. Publish a per-requirement report with commit SHA, commands, toolchain/grammar versions, corpus revisions, results, and reproducible failure logs. A global test count or line-coverage percentage is not requirement coverage.
- [ ] Preserve the gate and its baseline. Changes that remove requirements, tests, corpus cases, assertions, or required checks must be surfaced as scope changes requiring explicit maintainer approval, not ordinary ways to restore green CI.

### 3. Minimum behavioral acceptance matrix

Each row below needs concrete assertions, shared fixtures in both runtimes, and failure cases where applicable. This matrix supplements the atomic manifest; it does not replace any earlier requirement.

| Area | Required executable evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Default CST for every required language/path | Call the normal public parse API, without a special opt-in registry to hide missing defaults. Assert actual grammar nodes, hierarchy, named fields, child order, tokens/comments/trivia, exact UTF-8 spans, error/missing nodes, and embedded-language boundaries against an independent expected structure. Assert exact reconstruction separately. A root plus text, a nonzero node count, or a delimiter/token tree is insufficient. Include all aliases, advertised extension dispatch, dialects, importers, document/natural-language representations, and embedded paths. |
| Complete four-language syntax | Inventory the constructs of JavaScript, Rust, Lean, and Rocq/Coq against their claimed versions/editions. Run applicable upstream conformance/grammar corpora and representative real projects, not one example per grammar. Include modules, attributes, recursive definitions, macros/token trees, scoped notation, proof terms/tactics, Unicode, malformed input, recovery, and mixed-language files. Explain the mapping from each external corpus to the capability it actually tests. |
| Project-aware representation | Load multi-file projects, imports, dependencies, plugins, dialect settings, macros and notation. Verify scopes/symbol identity, module references, recursive definitions, types, effects, universes, proof structure, and surface-to-expansion/elaboration traces. Missing project context must give accurate diagnostics, not fabricated semantic success. Supplying valid context must enable the required behavior. |
| Structured transformations and construction | Exercise query, insert, delete, replace, move, clone, and construction from scratch through public APIs. Test sequences of edits and serialize/reload boundaries; verify tree integrity, updated spans, provenance/source mappings, diagnostics, and emitted source reparsing to the intended structure. Discarding the original string while replaying unchanged retained tokens is not sufficient: newly constructed and structurally changed programs must work. |
| Binding-safe transformations | Assert which declarations and references change, not only output text. Cover shadowing, nested scopes, qualified/module names, Unicode, macro-generated names, Lean/Rocq binders, capture avoidance, and unaffected comments/strings/regex literals. Preserve the distinction between syntax-only replacement and semantic refactoring. |

Fixing only the examples below is not completion.

### 1. Replace source-envelope “translation” with working semantic translation

Observed in the [JavaScript implementation](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/ced1a4c4ebd088854694b48c61f0013dd007d5a6/js/src/program-translation.js#L11) and [Rust implementation](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/ced1a4c4ebd088854694b48c61f0013dd007d5a6/rust/src/program_translation.rs#L101): translation hex-encodes the original source into a target-language comment and emits a dummy constant. The [contract](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/ced1a4c4ebd088854694b48c61f0013dd007d5a6/js/src/language-support.js#L119) reduces the observation to source recovery and assumes source-language execution after decoding. That is source transport, not the requested translation capability.

Independently reproduced using the JavaScript implementation at that exact commit:

- Rust input `pub fn answer() -> u32 { 42 }` translated to JavaScript exports only `__meta_language_portable_v1`; importing the emitted module yields no `answer()` or other callable implementation of the source function.
- JavaScript input `console.log(42);` translated to Rust emits only the encoded-source comment and `pub const __META_LANGUAGE_PORTABLE_V1: u32 = 1;`. It contains no implementation of the print operation.
- Source decoding succeeds. This proves that exact byte recovery does not establish behavioral preservation.

Required:

- [ ] Implement all 12 directed JavaScript/Rust/Lean/Rocq translation pairs in both runtime packages, through the shared meta-language representation.
- [ ] Emit working target-language implementations, or explicit operational encodings with their implemented target-side runtimes. The emitted program plus those runtimes must implement the source behavior. Merely assuming that a consumer decodes and runs the original source does not satisfy this requirement.
- [ ] Add regressions that execute translated computations and compare independently specified results, effects, errors, state changes, and termination behavior for the tested cases. Include the two examples above, recursion, control flow, data structures, modules, closures, and language-specific features from the complete required corpus.
- [ ] For proof-related translations, verify the translated proposition and proof under the declared faithful encoding, including preservation obligations. A kernel accepting a dummy constant proves nothing about the source theorem. Do not erase propositions, silently add axioms, or substitute a weaker observation contract.
- [ ] Exercise every pair in both packages with native target validation **and** semantic assertions. Compilation, exact decoding, round-trip source recovery, or agreement between two copies of the envelope implementation cannot alone pass a translation requirement.
- [ ] Add mutation tests replacing a real translation with the current comment-plus-constant implementation, a constant result, or an effect-erasing implementation. Each mutation must make the corresponding behavioral tests and aggregate gate fail.

The envelope may remain as a separately named serialization/transport facility; it must not satisfy semantic translation requirements.

[Module facts](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/ced1a4c4ebd088854694b48c61f0013dd007d5a6/js/src/program-representation.js#L475) label supplied dependency names as resolved.

Adding an unrelated or nonexistent dependency must not resolve an import or suppress its diagnostic. Test real multi-file projects, missing exports, conflicting names, shadowing, and capture avoidance.
- [ ] Produce and verify actual types, effects, universes, and elaborated structures required by each language. Check representative well-typed and ill-typed programs against independent language-toolchain results. A `resolved`/`elaborated` status field is not evidence.
- [ ] Implement the required macro/notation/plugin handling and expansion/elaboration provenance. Test genuine surface-to-expanded/elaborated relationships, including generated bindings and proof terms, rather than merely the presence of syntax markers.
- [ ] Exercise binding-safe transformations on those resolved structures and validate the resulting programs and proofs. Do not reclassify the missing semantic work as downstream RML responsibility; the previously specified upstream/downstream boundary remains unchanged.

issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #2293. `solve` told the AI, and in auto-restart mode posted restart comments claiming, that a PR/issue **title or description was edited after the last commit** when no human had edited anything:

- [relative-meta-logic#184](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic/pull/184): "Issue description (and title) edited", while issue #183 has **0** edits.
- [meta-language#196](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196): "Pull request description was edited after last commit". The only edit (02:56:07Z) was made by the previous AI session, which ran 20:34:20Z → 03:16:27Z.

Full analysis: [`docs/case-studies/issue-2293/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2293-cb811471f6cf/docs/case-studies/issue-2293/README.md)

## Root causes

1. **`updated_at` was treated as "content edited".** GitHub bumps it for comments, labels and cross-refs. In #196, a human *comment* at 18:24:36Z made the PR look edited.
2. **Solver edits were not told apart from human edits.** The solver and the maintainer share the `konard` login. Comments were filtered by tool markers; edits were not filtered at all.
3. **Self-referencing fallback.** With no `Fixes #N`, `issueNumber = prNumber`. The PR was then checked again as its own "issue", `Fixes #184` was written into PR #184, and the #2007 issue-snapshot check restarted on the AI's own title and body rewrites.

## Fix

- **New `src/description-edits.lib.mjs`**: reads the real edit history (GraphQL `userContentEdits` + `RenamedTitleEvent`). It builds *solver session windows* from tool comments: `AI Work Session Started/Resumed`, `🔄 Auto-restart N/M`, limit-reset resumes, and PR creation for the first session. It ignores bot edits and same-account edits inside a window. Another user's edit always counts.
- **`solve.feedback.lib.mjs`**: title/description feedback comes only from external edits, each listed with **evidence**:
  ```
  Pull request description was edited after last commit:
    - description edited at 2026-09-24T18:20:00.000Z by konard: +2/-0 lines (+ Please also support Kotlin.)
  ```
  Ignored edits and the reason each was skipped are logged under `--verbose`. The PR is not checked twice when it has no separate issue.
- **`solve.results.lib.mjs`**: no self-referencing `Fixes #<own number>`.
- **`solve.auto-merge.lib.mjs`** + **new `src/restart-evidence.lib.mjs`**:
  - the issue-metadata snapshot is skipped when the "issue" is the PR itself;
  - every restart reason is logged and posted with evidence: failing check names **with run URLs**, comment author/time/link/excerpt, and issue edit diffs;
  - restarts caused by the same failing checks are counted, flagged in the comment ("⚠️ The same checks have been failing for N restarts in a row.") and reported to the AI.
- **`solve.auto-merge-helpers.lib.mjs`**: `ci_failure` blocker details include run URLs.

Repeated CI failures are *flagged* rather than hard-stopped. A name-only signature cannot tell "still failing, but going 11/189 → 189/189" apart from "stuck", and the existing #2247 guard (`stopWhenSessionRepeated`) already stops sessions that made no progress.

## Reproduction and tests

`tests/test-issue-2293-description-edit-false-positive.mjs` (default suite) replays the real timestamps:

| Case | Expectation |
| --- | --- |
| A. #196: solver PR body edit inside its session | **no** edit feedback; the human comment is still counted |
| B. real human description + title edit | feedback with timestamp, editor, diff excerpt |
| C. issue with bumped `updated_at` and 0 `userContentEdits` | **no** feedback |
| D. `issueNumber === prNumber` (#184) | PR queried once, no `Fixes #184` self-link |
| E. session windows / classification | PR creation opens a session, "limit reached" does not, other users' edits count, bots don't |
| F. restart comment | failing checks + run URLs, edit diffs, repeated-failure warning |

On the old code, case A fails with exactly the incident's output: `["New comments on the pull request: 1","Pull request description was edited after last commit","Issue description was edited after last commit"]`.

The real edit histories are saved in `experiments/issue-2293/`, and replaying them through the new detector reports no false positives:
```
ml-196: 16 solver session windows, 45 edits, 45 ignored (solver/bot), 0 external
rml-184: 42 solver session windows, 78 edits, 78 ignored (solver/bot), 0 external
```

## CI: dependency-freshness refresh (unrelated to #2293)

`detect-changes` started failing on this branch because new upstream releases appeared (use-m 8.16.4, command-stream 1.1.0, links-notation 0.21.3, secretlint 13.0.6) and the freshness gate requires exact latest pins. The same failure hit #2297, which already contains a tested migration, so its two commits are cherry-picked here unchanged (only #2295-specific hunks and changeset dropped) to keep both branches consistent:

- `chore(deps): refresh CI-enforced dependency pins; adapt to command-stream 1.x results`: command-stream 1.x returns `stdout`/`stderr` as `CapturedReadable` streams that are truthy even when empty, so `result.stderr || fallback` reads become `result.stderr?.toString() || fallback`.
- `test: guard command-stream 1.x result semantics` (`tests/test-command-stream-1x-results.mjs`).

The guard also flagged one pattern in this PR's new `fetchContentEdits` (`src/description-edits.lib.mjs`), fixed in a follow-up commit.

## Out of scope / follow-ups (other subsystems)

- Container pruning, `keepContainer*` semantics, `$ --status` for removed containers: #2294
- `.gitconfig` single-file bind mount → `EBUSY` in `gh auth setup-git` (container launcher)
- Codex `RUST_LOG=debug` under `--verbose` and repeated plugin warnings (log noise)

issue.body:
Fixes #2303

## Problem

A 13h 38m docker session on link-foundation/meta-language#196 was reported as **"✅ Work session finished successfully"**, but it had been killed. Its writable layer reached 122.7 GB on a 192.7 GB host disk, which filled the disk. No auto-resume ran, and nothing was posted to the PR after "Auto-restart 2/5".

## Root cause

**start-command 0.34.0's detached watcher** (upstream: https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/174) runs:

```sh
docker logs -f C >> LOG; state=$(docker inspect C); if exit==0 && !oom then docker rm -f C; fi; footer; finalize
```

1. On a full disk, `docker logs -f >> LOG` fails with ENOSPC and returns while the container is **still running**.
2. `docker inspect` on a running container reports the zero values `ExitCode 0` and `FinishedAt 0001-01-01…`.
3. The watcher therefore `rm -f`s the live container (this is the actual kill), writes `Exit Code: 0`, and finalizes the record as `executed / 0`.
4. The only trace left is `endTimeSource: "observed-at"`. Containers that really exited have `docker-finished-at`.

Hive Mind trusted that exit 0. Its disk evidence also came only from log markers that were 50 minutes old, and the disk was free again once the layer was removed.

Full timeline, requirements, root causes and research: [`docs/case-studies/issue-2303/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2303-928b0c381ae1/docs/case-studies/issue-2303/README.md).

## Changes

- **`src/session-monitor.unobserved-exit.lib.mjs`**: a docker session that reports success with `endTimeSource: observed-at` is reclassified as **killed** (`exitCode null`). The original values are kept as `reportedExitCode` / `reportedStatus`. Because it is a kill, the existing kill diagnosis and the `--on-session-kill=resume` recovery (#2134/#2189) now run: a fresh `solve … --resume <tool session>`.
- **`src/session-monitor.host-disk.lib.mjs`**: every monitor tick runs one `fs.promises.statfs()` on the log's filesystem and records the **lowest** free space seen. The value is persisted across bot restarts and used as disk-full evidence.
- **`session-kill-diagnostics`**: an `ENOSPC` / "No space left on device" line in the log counts as disk-full evidence. Evidence lines explain why the reported success was not trusted.
- **Headline** names the cause: `❌ Work session killed (disk full)`. All locales use a `{{reason}}` template.
- A failed `$ --status` query keeps the session tracked instead of being reported as a success (`running:false, exitCode:null` used to read as ✅). After `STATUS_QUERY_ERROR_LIMIT` (20) consecutive failures it is reported as failed.
- A container that the watcher already removed is no longer advertised as "Docker container kept".
- Verbose logs added for each new decision.
- `chore(deps)`: refreshed the pins required by CI's dependency-freshness gate: formal-ai 0.352.1, use-m 8.16.4, command-stream 1.1.0, links-notation 0.21.3, secretlint 13.0.6 and lint-staged 17.6.0.

## How to reproduce

- `node experiments/issue-2303-watcher-enospc.mjs` needs docker and `alpine:3.20`. It runs the real start-command watcher with the log on `/dev/full`. Result: the live container is removed, and `$ --status` shows `executed`, `exitCode 0`, `endTimeSource observed-at`.
- `node tests/test-issue-2303-unobserved-docker-exit.mjs` (51 assertions) covers the incident end to end: a docker session with 0.1 GB of host disk free, then `executed/0/observed-at`. Expected result:
  - "Work session killed (disk full)" with kill diagnostics.
  - A `--resume` recovery session is launched.
  - No "container kept" section and no removal attempt.

## Upstream

- https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/174: the watcher removes a running container after `docker logs -f` fails. The same issue covers the `code || 0` fallbacks that turn signal kills into exit 0.

body:
## Completion audit, 2026-09-27: 112 pre-merge requirements still fail; finish implementation and add automatic cache cleanup

Audited PR head `df0b04865b1a07db3bac4b530953fd7b885523e6`, the original issue and requirement-bearing comments, the latest acceptance artifact, public entry points, and repository CI/hook configuration. This PR is **not complete**.

**All implementation and verification needed for the full requested scope is already authorized. Complete it in PR #196. Do not ask for another scope decision, wait for approval, reduce requirements, or move work to follow-up PRs.** This includes the new resource-cleanup requirement below. The [earlier delivery directive](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5819788893) and [maintainer's continued full-delivery instruction](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5836875663) remain in force.

### Verified current status — use the current report, not the stale description

The [latest full acceptance run](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36225143951), on merge candidate `4b14611712b57563567ad679543e2b572f84cd85`, reports **77/189 pre-merge requirements passing, 112 failing; 257/481 verification cells passing, 224 failing; zero gate errors**. Its [downloadable per-requirement report](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36225143951/artifacts/10900352945) identifies the exact missing assertions.

The passing requirement groups are 57 inventoried default-CST targets, 5 embedded-language cases, 4 native-validator requirements, and 11 gate fault-injection requirements. This is real progress; it is neither all-language coverage nor complete semantic delivery. The PR description still cites an older 11/189 result and needs synchronization. The three publication requirements are outside this pre-merge count and must also be delivered.

Every currently failing group must be completed:

| Required area | Failing atomic requirements | Work still requiring accepted behavioral evidence |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Full four-language semantics | 40 | Scope/binding, imports/modules, project/dependency context, recursion, types/universes, effects, attributes, macros/notation, proof/tactic representation where applicable, and expansion/elaboration provenance. |
| Structured transformations | 32 | Query, construct, insert, delete, replace, move, clone, and emit for all four languages, including structure and source-map integrity across edit/serialization sequences. |
| Directed translations | 12 | Every directed pair among JavaScript, Rust, Lean, and Rocq, with actual behavior/type/proof preservation, faithful encodings and their implemented runtimes. |
| External conformance | 4 | Construct inventory mapped to executed pinned upstream corpora and real projects, including malformed input, Unicode, and mixed-language cases. |
| Generative testing | 4 | Required property/fuzz/metamorphic assertions for the four languages. |
| Grammar importers | 5 | ABNF, BNF, EBNF, Pest, and tree-sitter grammar JSON: actual importer behavior and acceptance observations. |
| Cross-runtime parity | 5 | CSTs, diagnostics, semantics, transformations, and translations. |
| Binding-safe rename | 4 | Full applicable binding/capture/project-context cases across all four languages, not only the recently fixed JavaScript examples. |
| Shared concepts/provenance/schema | 3 | Shared semantics without collapsing language-specific distinctions, stable schema/extension contracts, and provenance. |
| Candidate package/RML delivery | 3 | All three candidate requirements still lack the observed `supportedPlatforms` assertion, despite successful platform-consumer jobs. Diagnose and fix the execution/evidence join; do not manufacture a pass. |

Missing observations do not prove that every associated implementation is absent. They do mean the requirement has not been verified. For each row, distinguish missing implementation from missing meaningful tests or broken result ingestion, then fix all applicable parts. Do not satisfy an assertion by registering a callback that merely repeats its label.

### Concrete implementation and integration gaps

1. **The public translator still bypasses the new portable-core implementation.** The [package export](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/df0b04865b1a07db3bac4b530953fd7b885523e6/js/src/index.js) exposes [`translateProgram`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/df0b04865b1a07db3bac4b530953fd7b885523e6/js/src/program-translation.js#L19), whose positive behavior is still two exact regex-recognized forms. I independently ran:
   - `translateProgram('console.log(42);', 'JavaScript', 'Rust')` → executable print, `semantic-subset`.
   - The semantically equivalent `'console.log(42);\n'` → `portable-encoding` and a dummy constant.
   - `'console.log(6 * 7);'` → the same transport-only result.
   
   The new frontends/checker/emitters in `js/src/translation/` and `rust/src/translation/` are substantial progress, but must be integrated into the stable public API, type declarations, installed-package tests, links-based representation/transformation pipeline, all 12 pair tests, and RML consumers. Internal stage tests are not public delivery. Add the whitespace/expression regressions above and nontrivial computations/effects/proofs through the **installed public APIs in both packages**.

2. **The new checker is a subset, not full language support.** For example, its [checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/df0b04865b1a07db3bac4b530953fd7b885523e6/js/src/translation/check.js) reject higher-order application, partial application, certain data-value comparisons, narrowing integer casts, and natural `n + k` patterns above 16. The JavaScript frontend rejects ordinary unannotated functions unless JSDoc types are supplied; I reproduced that on a valid `function apply(f, x) { return f(x); }` program. Implement the required constructs/faithful encodings, inference/context handling, ownership/effects/universes, and proof-preservation contracts. Keep truthful diagnostics while working, but never count those diagnostics as delivery of the requested positive behavior.

3. **Stage parity is explicitly disabled.** [`every_translation_stage_matches_the_javascript_pipeline`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/df0b04865b1a07db3bac4b530953fd7b885523e6/rust/tests/unit/translation_stages.rs#L138) is still `#[ignore]`. Resolve the recorded parse/diagnostic mismatches, enable the complete test in ordinary required CI, and preserve independent semantic oracles: identical snapshots generated from one implementation are insufficient by themselves. I ran the five dependency-free JavaScript checker/stage-fixture tests successfully; that does not replace full JS/Rust native and public-API parity.

4. **57 registered targets do not mean all existing languages.** The [catalog](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/df0b04865b1a07db3bac4b530953fd7b885523e6/js/src/language-catalog.js) has 57 entries; Haskell, OCaml, and Zig are absent. The [normal parse API](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/df0b04865b1a07db3bac4b530953fd7b885523e6/js/src/network.js#L41) still returns a lossless-text fallback outside its recognized parser dispatch. Extend actual default grammar coverage and the maintained conformance inventory; no caller opt-in, text fallback, registry entry, or fixed shortlist may be used to claim complete default CST support.

5. **Full project semantics remain incomplete.** The [contracts](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/df0b04865b1a07db3bac4b530953fd7b885523e6/docs/four-language-contracts.md) still correctly distinguish lexical/surface facts from complete module/export resolution, typing, macro expansion, and proof elaboration. Connect and extend the new semantic core to the actual public representation, structured edits, and project loader. Preserve the phantom-dependency, capture, property-key, destructuring, and hoisted-`var` regressions already added. Test real multi-file projects, generated bindings, invalid typing, and nontrivial proof structures against independent expected outcomes.

6. **Required CI failures remain.** [Rust CI](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36224139901) fails the 1000-line file limit for `translation/{emit_rust,rust,check,ir,rocq,emit_rocq,javascript}.rs`, and its `cargo llvm-cov --fail-under-lines 84.30` step exits unsuccessfully. Refactor and add meaningful tests; do not weaken thresholds, ignore required tests, or label these out-of-scope housekeeping.

7. **Distribution remains unfinished.** `npm view meta-language version --json` still returns `0.46.0`; the PR package version is `0.58.2`. Complete matching usable npm/crate delivery and current downstream RML integration. Fix the platform evidence join, validate packed and published artifacts in clean consumers, and exercise the new public capabilities—not merely importability or parsing two examples. Three release-delivery rows remain outside the 189 pre-merge total. Remove the renewed `Fixes #195` while delivery is incomplete; metadata must not auto-close unfinished work.

### New mandatory requirement: automatic, safe cleanup of all build-cache classes

Development is consuming excessive disk. Implement this in this PR, not as a follow-up. Use the working patterns in formal-ai at `d209aac6`: [installed commit hook](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/d209aac6461b355f1a527831202af3423135f7e6/.githooks/pre-commit), [pre-commit integration](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/d209aac6461b355f1a527831202af3423135f7e6/.pre-commit-config.yaml), [build-cache pruning](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/d209aac6461b355f1a527831202af3423135f7e6/scripts/prune-build-cache.sh), [test wrapper](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/d209aac6461b355f1a527831202af3423135f7e6/scripts/cargo-test.sh), and [disk-policy checks](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai/blob/d209aac6461b355f1a527831202af3423135f7e6/scripts/check-disk-usage-policy.rs). Its useful principles are fingerprint-aware stale-artifact cleanup, a default local size budget, cleanup after failed as well as successful tests, bounded development profiles, and hooks that actually get installed. Adapt these principles to this repository; do not blindly copy host-wide deletion commands.

- [ ] Register this new obligation in the requirement manifest/ledger with implementation, event coverage, behavioral safety tests, and measured disk evidence. Existing totals are baselines, not a ceiling on requirements.
- [ ] Provide one documented cleanup entry point covering **every regenerable build-cache class this repository creates**: Rust targets across debug/release/test/coverage, incremental and linked example artifacts; JS build/test caches and temporary package consumers; generated parser/compiler build intermediates; Lean/Rocq build output; acceptance/benchmark scratch trees; and project-owned container/BuildKit caches where used. Include nested temporary clones and package-build target directories, not only the main `rust/target`.
- [ ] Run cleanup on **every pre-commit**, including documentation-only commits. Wire it into the normal developer bootstrap and verify installation on a fresh clone; a committed but uninstalled hook configuration is insufficient. Respect and compose with existing hooks. Do not modify a downstream consumer's Git configuration when this project is installed/built as a dependency.
- [ ] Also run cleanup at build/test/coverage/benchmark/package/acceptance completion and CI teardown, including failure and safely handled interruption. Use exit/finally handling, preserve the original command's exit status, stop or wait for owned child processes, and archive required logs/artifacts before removing scratch output. Provide a pre-run low-disk check and explicit full-clean mode.
- [ ] Sweep stale/disposable outputs across all those cache classes and enforce a documented configurable **aggregate disk budget**, with before/after/reclaimed-byte reporting. A small warm cache may be retained within that budget as in formal-ai; repeatedly retaining every historic target tree is not cleanup. Full-clean mode must remove all registered regenerable build caches. Document any temporary debug override; normal development must clean automatically.
- [ ] Reduce avoidable growth: bounded build/test concurrency, lean development/test debug and incremental settings, compile-only checks where executing/linking examples is unnecessary, reuse compatible build outputs, and bounded compiler-cache policy instead of repeatedly archiving unbounded target trees. Preserve all required feature/platform/behavior coverage.
- [ ] Make cleanup repository-scoped, idempotent, concurrency-safe, and portable across the supported OSes. Validate paths and ownership, reject traversal/symlink escape, and account safely for custom target directories. Never delete source, tracked vendored grammars, fixtures, proof/corpus data, uncommitted work, active-build outputs, another worktree's artifacts, or evidence still needed by the acceptance gate. Do not purge global Cargo/npm caches, unrelated Docker resources, or volumes; use project ownership/labels.
- [ ] Add executable tests for fresh-clone hook installation, pre-commit on a non-code change, all cache classes, repeated runs, success/failure/interruption, missing cleanup tools, paths with spaces, custom target directories, active parallel builds/worktrees, budget enforcement, and source/evidence preservation. CI must detect disabled hooks/wrappers or omitted cache categories. Use temporary fixtures, not the developer's real caches.
- [ ] Show measured before/after disk usage for a representative development/acceptance cycle and prove the subsequent clean rebuild and full verification still pass. Cleanup itself must not create passing test evidence or hide a failure.


### Completion and anti-bypass requirements

Keep every prior requirement and its intended meaning. Add this comment's obligations to the atomic manifest, preserving stable IDs and source links. Maintain required per-assertion observed execution, exact commit/fixture/toolchain identity, negative cases, and end-to-end mutation tests. A green native validator for a dummy constant is not translation; a capability label is not elaboration; a test filename or suite exit is not requirement evidence.

For every failing cell, implement the actual behavior and independent assertion, run it, prove that removal/corruption is detected, and regenerate the report from those observations. Finish all pre-merge and delivery obligations, plus cleanup, in this PR. Keep working while gaps remain; do not stop at updating the ledger, repairing CI alone, publishing this backlog, or requesting human direction.

issue.body:
## Status

This PR advances #183 but does not complete it. The audited ledger in `docs/case-studies/issue-183/requirements.md` holds 151 atomic requirements: 95 complete, 32 partial, 21 open, and 3 blocked. The full-closure acceptance gate (R149), full-language closure, link-executed verification across the whole corpus, comparable alternative foundations, and the native meta-theory workflow remain open.

This description covers the most recent work, newest first. Every requirement, with its status and evidence, is in the ledger.

## What changed

### Replacing a linked definition of K1 (R150 partial, R149 and R151 open)

Review `5836717056` asks for an executable witness that the semantics comes from linked definitions: run D on an unchanged generic runtime, replace D with D′, and get execution according to D′. The mirrored `executes a replaced linked definition of K1 on the unchanged runtime` tests in `js/tests/linked-program.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/linked_program_tests.rs` replace one rule of `links-meta-foundation` in `lib/meta-theory/universal.lino` at a time and run the same request through the same runtime:

| Mechanism (rule replaced) | Under D | Under D′ |
|---|---|---|
| matching (`match-repeated-variable`) | `(pair (atom a) (atom b))` | `(atom same)` |
| substitution (`substitute-pair`, mirrored) | `(pair (atom a) (atom done))` | `(pair (atom done) (atom a))` |
| rule selection (`select-next-object-rule`) | `(atom second)` | `(atom a)` |
| verification (`verify-object-result`) | `verified` | `(verified (atom a))` |

In every case the replaced rule fires, and the host operations under D and D′ are the same four: `contract-k-link`, `contract-s-link`, `enforce-cycle-and-resource-bounds`, and `parse-linked-forms`. The runtime sources and the compiled `fixed-point.ski` never name the constructors those rules use (`meta-substitute`, `finish-meta-apply`, `select-meta-rewrite`, `rewrite-miss`, `binding-found`, `match-ok`), so no host branch decides what the replaced definitions do. `experiments/definition-replacement/k1-replacement.mjs` prints the same comparison.

The witness does not yet reach substitution itself. The `keeps K0 substitution fixed when K1 substitution is replaced` tests show that once `substitute-pair` is mirrored, K1 interpreting an encoded copy of its own rule disagrees with direct execution, and direct execution still gives `(match-ok (no-bindings))`. Direct execution substitutes inside the compiled S/K kernel, and replacing that definition means regenerating the artifact, not loading a new linked definition. R150 is therefore Partial.

The review's acceptance gate is registered as R149 (Open): at least two different minimal meta-foundations, each showing closure, substitutability, semantic preservation, minimality relative to the witness, no hidden host authority, self-interpretation, and a complete trust boundary. The S/K `6/6` witness is recorded as the current implementation bootstrap, not completion, and one reduced foundation has no comparable peer. R151 (Open) records that the parser, elaborator, compiler, and code generation are still host code, so full implementation closure has not been reached.

### One LiNo front end for both runtimes

Both runtimes now read every `.lino` document through one front end, `js/src/rml-lino-frontend.mjs` and its Rust mirror `rust/src/lino_frontend.rs`, instead of calling `links-notation` 0.20 directly. The front end:

- reads every reference that opens with a quote itself, in one left-to-right pass, and hands the parser a token in its place;
- hands the parser no piece whose parentheses nest more than two levels deep (`LINO_PIECE_DEPTH`), putting a one-name placeholder where a deeper group stood;
- refuses a document nested deeper than 64 parenthesis-and-indentation levels (`MAX_LINO_NESTING_DEPTH`) or longer than `MAX_LINO_SOURCE_UNITS` code units, with the parse error `E006`;
- builds the links of an indented id itself: a line under an indented id keeps its name, and an indented id among those lines reads the way it reads on its own, so `a:` over `b: c` reads as `(a: (b: c))`; a line indented under any other line of an indented id is refused with `E006` instead of being dropped.

`js/tests/lino-frontend.test.mjs` and `rust/tests/lino_frontend_tests.rs` check the same 100 cases in `test-corpus/lino-frontend/cases.json`, read 64 indented ids nested one under another and refuse 65, read twelve sources built to be slow within five seconds each, and keep references made of private-use characters apart from the names the front end makes. `experiments/lino-frontend/differential.mjs`, `deep-documents.mjs`, `quote-reading.mjs`, and `nested-indented-ids.mjs` compare the two front ends over generated documents and find no difference.

### Upstream links-notation reports

Reading `links-notation` 0.20 directly on these shapes is why the front end exists. `experiments/lino-frontend/upstream.mjs` shows, in both runtimes, what the parser reads alone and how long it takes. The findings are filed against `link-foundation/links-notation`:

- #312 - the JavaScript and Rust parsers disagree on a lone CR, Unicode spaces, a last line of spaces, and singlets;
- #313 - lines under an indented id lose their names and their own indented lines;
- #314 - reading nested groups takes time that grows exponentially with the nesting in both ports, and the Rust `parse_lino_to_links` entry point adds quadratic time by deep-copying the subtree once per level;
- #315 - a deeply nested document overflows the Rust stack and aborts the process uncatchably, and neither port enforces the nesting-depth limit it documents;
- #316 - reading a reference that opens with a wide run of quotes takes quadratic time in both ports.

The three denial-of-service reports, #314 through #316, were filed after the maintainer authorized public reporting (PR comments 5831221597 and 5831357798). The front end already caps source size and nesting depth and reads quoted references itself, so both runtimes stay away from these shapes.

### Selectable type ontology (R129 complete, R114 partial)

`recursive-type-ontology.md` and the mirrored `linkCliInteropProfile` / `link_cli_interop_profile` tests classify the opt-in link-cli type ontology as a candidate default construction, not a premise about what links intrinsically are or a logical `Type : Type` rule (R129, complete). The default is available only through an explicit factory; the mirrored `leaves the default type ontology to the callers that select it` tests find no `Type` link in a bare typed network, no runtime module that selects the default ontology, and an evaluator whose universes stay stratified, answering `Type of Type` only for a source that declares `(Type: Type Type)`. Foundation-declared universe and soundness contracts remain open (R114, partial).

### Foundational orientation audit (R148)

Review `5823272578` is registered as R148 (Partial), with the "Where consequence orientation can come from" section added to `foundation-search.md`. The mirrored `orientationAudit` / `orientation_audit` tests ask where the orientation of a consequence could come from without assuming source/target, premise/conclusion, time, rewrite direction, function/argument, cause/effect, truth, or proof, and separate intrinsic asymmetries from observer-chosen ones across automorphism-distinguished structures, same-observation pairs, renaming, faithful representations, and carrier recursion. The result is a finite no-go, `CONSEQUENCE_ORIENTATION_DISTINGUISHED_BUT_NOT_FORCED`: address equality and slot order separate the two candidate orientations but never rank them, because composing any invariant selector with the output swap gives an invariant selector that chooses the opposite orientation. R147 stays Partial; an intrinsic orientation of consequence remains open.

### PR metadata

The description ends with `Advances #183` and names no issue in a closing directive, because #183 is not complete. A step in `tests.yml` runs on every PR 184 event, reads the live description through the API, and removes any whole-line closing directive in every GitHub form (`#N`, `owner/repo#N`, or the issue URL, with an optional colon and trailing period), writing only when something changed and failing if a directive appears inside other text. Its tests cover the updated, unchanged, inline-refusal, and other-PR paths.

## Verification

- `node --test scripts/foundation-search.test.mjs scripts/issue-183-requirements.test.mjs`
- `npm test` in `js/` (1506 passed)
- `cargo test --all-targets` in `rust/` (942 passed)
- `npm run lint:english`, `npm run test:bootstrap`, `npm run report:bootstrap-metrics`, and `npm run report:foundation-search` in `js/`

The finite no-go covers address equality and slot order under the named, anonymous, and unordered contracts and adds no direction bit; it does not exclude a more primitive Links property outside those observations. A host-free generic principle that derives a consequence from its premises, an intrinsic continuation law, implication, execution, and law-level self-application all remain open.

Advances #183

## What remains for full delivery — audit of `c5eb2303`, 2026-09-28

**PR #196 is not complete. The remaining work is not just the eight red rows in the current matrix.** It also includes the original full-language/full-semantics scope that the current portable-core tests do not establish, the three published-delivery requirements, and the explicitly requested automatic cache cleanup that has not been registered or delivered.

### Progress since the previous audit

The public API now invokes the portable-core frontends/checker/emitters. Translation-stage parity is no longer ignored. Required Rust lint/format, coverage, and package-build checks now pass. The platform-report join was repaired; importer, transformation, rename, project-context, parity and translation-corpus evidence has increased substantially. These are real improvements, not the old implementation being restated.

The [latest acceptance run](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36387613279), on merge candidate `81965bfbbf509885acc060e1e892e4a734ba09ab`, reports **181/189 pre-merge requirements passing, 8 failing; 465/481 cells passing, 16 failing; zero gate errors**. I inspected its [actual report artifact](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36387613279/artifacts/10955298956), not the stale PR description.

### 1. Finish the eight currently failing requirements with actual execution

| Exact requirement ID | Area | Missing runtime evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `I195-CONFORMANCE-javascript` | external-conformance | JavaScript and Rust |
| `I195-CONFORMANCE-lean` | external-conformance | JavaScript and Rust |
| `I195-CONFORMANCE-rocq` | external-conformance | JavaScript and Rust |
| `I195-CONFORMANCE-rust` | external-conformance | JavaScript and Rust |
| `I195-GENERATIVE-javascript` | generative-testing | JavaScript and Rust |
| `I195-GENERATIVE-lean` | generative-testing | JavaScript and Rust |
| `I195-GENERATIVE-rocq` | generative-testing | JavaScript and Rust |
| `I195-GENERATIVE-rust` | generative-testing | JavaScript and Rust |

- [ ] **Conformance:** for each language and runtime, map the claimed construct/version inventory to executed pinned upstream corpora and representative real projects; record corpus provenance; exercise malformed recovery, Unicode and mixed-language cases. The current report lacks execution records for all seven required assertions in each cell. Grammar patches, experiments and a sweep that finds no error nodes are useful work, but are not the complete conformance contract: check independently expected CST structure, fields, trivia, spans, diagnostics and relevant semantics too.
- [ ] **Generative testing:** execute property-based, fuzz and metamorphic cases covering round trips, malformed input, Unicode spans and edit sequences, with an independent oracle. All eight required assertions in each cell currently lack observed execution. Register reproducible seeds/corpus identities and keep failure reproducers.
- [ ] Integrate these into required CI and its observed assertion reports in both packages. Do not make them pass by copying expectations into callbacks, testing only the implemented subset, or treating self-consistency as an independent oracle.

### 2. Finish full language support beyond the portable core

The twelve translation requirements now pass for the pinned corpus. **That does not establish complete translation of the requested languages.** I ran the current [public translator implementation](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/c5eb23036ee30e2095c406a44d080e3a3e10ff51/js/src/program-translation.js) directly at this head:

| JavaScript input → Rust | Actual result |
| --- | --- |
| `console.log(6n * 7n);\n` | `semantic-translation` — the new core is used. |
| `console.log(42);` | Legacy `semantic-subset` special case. |
| `console.log(42);\n` | `portable-encoding`; JavaScript Number is outside the core. |
| `console.log(6 * 7);` | `portable-encoding`; JavaScript Number is outside the core. |
| `function answer() { return 42; } console.log(answer());` | `portable-encoding`; requires JSDoc annotations. |

Preserve each compatible source's unique valid coverage; do not indiscriminately union dialects, accept invalid combinations or erase disagreements to improve a score.
- [ ] Test deterministic/reproducible output, idempotence, semantic stability under input reordering, incremental re-merging after upstream changes, conflict resolution, no duplicate canonical identities for established equivalences, and preserved language/edition boundaries. Where explicit precedence between sources is needed, encode a reproducible rule justified by language specifications and independent evidence.
- [ ] Define “best possible” with evidence: construct coverage and correctness first, preservation of unique features and shared reuse, then measured recovery quality, execution time and memory. Publish comparisons against the inventoried source grammars; do not claim superiority merely from passing the same self-generated fixtures.

### 6. Readable English names, enforced by tests

- [ ] Prefer self-explanatory English **noun phrases for concepts and verb phrases for operations/relations**, with no abbreviations in canonical concept names. For example, prefer “expression”, “statement”, “function declaration” and “resolve reference” over “expr”, “stmt”, “fn decl” and “resolve ref”.
- [ ] Give every canonical concept a stable identity, readable phrase, meaning/definition, applicable constraints and source aliases. Language-specific tokens, external identifiers and original names must remain lossless provenance/aliases; do not translate source code or destroy round trips to enforce the canonical naming convention.
- [ ] Build automatic naming/renaming into import and merge, then enforce vocabulary, phrase role, abbreviation expansion, collision/duplicate checks and full inventory coverage in CI. Add positive/negative fixtures, including deliberately abbreviated, ambiguous and duplicate names. A letters-only regular expression or a hand-picked example list is insufficient to establish readability or semantic uniqueness.

### 7. Complete semantics and downstream integration, not only grammars

- [ ] Retain and finish full JavaScript, Rust, Lean and Rocq representation/transformation and all **12 directed translations in both runtime packages** through the common editable links representation. Complete the construct/project inventory, including classes/objects, arrays and mutation, standard-library behavior, imports, higher-order functions, asynchronous behavior, ownership, macros/notation, types/universes/effects and proofs/tactics.
- [ ] Finish binding-safe edits, project elaboration and hygiene, faithful errors/aborts/overflow/effects, source mappings and real proof-preservation obligations. Faithful target encodings and runtimes are required where concepts are not native. Unsupported diagnostics, non-aborting-only claims, source pass-through, or bounded theorem checks remain incomplete rather than substitute implementations.
- [ ] Audit concrete requirements and usage in [relative-meta-logic](https://github.com/link-foundation/relative-meta-logic/pull/184) and [formal-ai](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai), and commit a consumer-to-capability/test matrix. The supplied `link-foundation/formal-ai` URL currently returns 404; the accessible project is `link-assistant/formal-ai`, referenced earlier in this discussion. Use that actual consumer, not a nonexistent integration target.
- [ ] Verify downstream parse → common links → semantic transformation/translation → emission workflows using clean installed artifacts, including shared concept reuse and preservation of language-specific distinctions. Cover both consumers' actual workloads, not only demonstration strings. Meta-language must supply their reusable language infrastructure without taking over RML's foundation/proof authority.

### 8. Independent, comprehensive acceptance — no loophole through a smaller manifest

- [ ] Expand the atomic ledger and required CI to cover every obligation above, in addition to all earlier requirements. Separate grammar feature coverage, Links Notation compatibility, native execution, import/export/round trips, automatic merge/deduplication/renaming, naming quality, concrete/abstract tree fidelity, semantics/translations, downstream integration, dependency freshness and documentation consistency.
- [ ] Run native merged grammars against the pinned **independent** ANTLR, tree-sitter and relevant official parser/compiler/prover corpora and real projects. Use multiple oracles where available. Trace each construct and source discrepancy to a test and justified resolution; neither one upstream parser nor a popular grammar is automatically the complete language specification.
- [ ] Run shared JavaScript/Rust conformance, property/fuzz/metamorphic tests, malformed/recovery cases, Unicode/layout/embedded syntax, grammar mutation, edit sequences and large real projects. Preserve seeds, revisions, outputs and minimal reproducers. Check actual assertions executed, not only test registration or fixture hashes.
- [ ] Prove the native dependency boundary by testing installed production packages with external grammar engines and oracle assets absent. Change a native linked grammar rule and show that parsing changes accordingly without an unrelated host-code patch; this must exercise the actual public parse path.
- [ ] Add gate-mutation tests: removing a grammar feature, leaving an old dependency, bypassing native execution, breaking reverse conversion, introducing a semantic duplicate or abbreviation, dropping a source requirement, weakening an oracle mapping, or replacing real proof obligations with bounded checks must make the relevant gate fail.
- [ ] Keep the full coverage inventory independent of the implemented subset. No silent exclusions, deleted languages/features, skipped cells, unobserved assertions, fabricated evidence or changed acceptance definitions to obtain green results. Document what finite tests establish separately from universal correctness claims.

### 9. Preserve cleanup, finish publication, and report completion truthfully

- [ ] Retain the complete earlier cache policy across pre-commit (including documentation-only commits), build/test/coverage/benchmark/package/acceptance events and CI teardown, including failure/interruption. Extend it to imported grammar corpora, generator/oracle builds and merged-grammar caches. Apply aggregate budgets, low-disk preflight, bounded concurrency and safe full-clean with measured recovery/rebuild tests.
- [ ] Preserve canonical native grammar sources, fixtures/licenses, uncommitted work, active builds and verification evidence. Validate ownership and paths; never solve disk usage by deleting global/user caches or unrelated container data. Keep regenerable cache cleanup separate from removing obsolete production architecture.
- [ ] Complete matching usable npm/crates releases and clean downstream delivery evidence, including the existing `I195-DELIVERY-NPM-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-CRATE-PUBLISHED` and `I195-DELIVERY-RML-PUBLISHED` requirements and formal-ai consumption. Candidate builds or a future publication workflow are not proof that users can install the delivered capabilities.
- [ ] Reconcile README, architecture/vision, source register, generated ledger, PR body and release reports with actual evidence. Remove premature issue-closing directives and do not claim full completion while any required work remains.

**Completion means the entire repository implements this vision, all issue/PR requirements are recorded and independently verified, and the delivered artifacts support the consumers. It does not mean only that today's 219 rows are green. Complete the implementation–verification loop in this single PR; no further maintainer response is needed.**
