issue.body:
## Summary

Fixes #2301. The analysis covers all three production runs: [links-notation#315](https://github.com/link-foundation/links-notation/pull/319) (Claude Code 2.1.282), [browser-commander#106](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/konard/public-logs/main/tmp-hive-mind-log-upload-2nNBS9/08e10c4fbb284728/sanitized.log.txt) (2.1.284, 2.5 h, 15 subagents) and its [re-run](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/konard/97c3a1eb9c57b52512e3a999724cccf8/raw/6e1935a7b02d6a0efc1c6250b4985954debbc32f/tmp-hive-mind-log-upload-zYtTNW-sanitized.log.txt) (2.1.284, 44 min, 4 subagents). It also used the installed Claude binary and live reproductions.

### Exact root cause

Claude Code print mode waits for background tasks only up to `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` (default 600000). The ceiling counts from the main thread's last message, not from the tasks' progress. In all three incidents, exactly 600 s after that message, it:

1. printed `Background tasks still running after 600s; terminating.` to stderr;
2. stopped every task, even subagents that were still working (in the re-run one had started `pytest` 2 s earlier, log line 155713);
3. gave the killed subagents synthetic `[Request interrupted by user]` and `The user doesn't want to proceed with this tool use` results;
4. still emitted `result: success` (in the re-run, all three held-back results at once) and exited 0.

No user, permission prompt or tool classifier was involved. Hive Mind then let those **subagent-scoped** events (`parent_tool_use_id`) become the main session's final tool result. It reported `Final tool result failed … / Claude command failed with exit code 0` and never continued the work.

### Fixes

- **Background work stays enabled, with 4x the wait.** `solve` sets `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=2400000` (40 min, 4x Claude Code's default; `HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS` overrides it). It is deliberately not `0`, which would let one stuck task hang `solve` forever. The earlier `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_*` approach is removed.
- **Silent auto-resume when the ceiling is still hit.** The sweep is detected exactly (`src/claude.print-turn.lib.mjs`). This removes three false negatives:
  - stops that arrive before the `result`;
  - the stderr ceiling line was not recognised;
  - a background Bash is killed about 4 s after `result` with `killed.system=0`.

  `solve` then resumes the same session up to 5 times in a row (`HIVE_MIND_CLAUDE_INCOMPLETE_TURN_MAX_RESUMES`). Each resume is only logged, with no PR comment or notice. The prompt tells the model that the ceiling (not a user) cancelled the work, lists the cancelled tasks with their partial output files, and asks it to redo only what is missing and to run long work in the foreground. The stale kill that Claude Code replays at the start of a `--resume` does not trigger another resume. A model's own `TaskStop` and later main-thread turns are handled correctly.
- **No false positives from subagents** (`src/claude.stream-events.lib.mjs`). Subagent tool errors, cancellations, last messages and compaction summaries no longer become the main session's verdict or summary; they are logged as diagnostics. The failure wording is now `Claude session failed (the CLI itself exited with code 0): …`.
- **OOM follow-ups (incident 1).** A failed session affected by a child OOM (`OOMKilled` + exit 1) is resumed through `--on-session-kill=resume`. The notice reports a new session only after it actually starts, and includes its ID. Telegram Docker tasks default to a 25% host-memory limit.
- The Claude prompt says that background work is allowed but only waited for within the ceiling after the turn ends, so long work belongs in the foreground.

The [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2301-1462dcec50ad/docs/case-studies/issue-2301/README.md) has:

- all three timelines with log line numbers;
- the binary evidence;
- an audit of every error and warning in the logs.

Most entries are expected or recoverable, such as the 46 worktree-guard refusals, the model's own command errors, and the `--attach-logs` security notice. It also has the compressed logs and upstream references.

**Upstream:** [anthropics/claude-code#98170](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/98170) is a focused report. It covers the idle-based ceiling killing working subagents, `success`/exit 0 after cancelled work, "user" wording, uncounted Bash tasks, results held back until exit, and the stale replay on `--resume`, with the repro, workarounds and suggested fixes. It is cross-linked on [#85066](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/85066#issuecomment-5892348970), next to the earlier follow-ups ([1](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/85066#issuecomment-5842704259), [2](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/85066#issuecomment-5885429221)).

## Incident 4: link-foundation/meta-language#196 ([review](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2302#issuecomment-5895702312))

The solve log and the bot log are private, so only sanitized excerpts are in the case study. Every symptom was traced to its cause:

| Symptom | Root cause | Fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| No log on the failure; `RPC failed; HTTP 408` for a 165 MB log, and nothing on the PR | gh-upload-log 0.9.2 pushes once, without a retry; a failed attach was not reported | Retry with backoff, then upload complete line-aligned parts. If that also fails, a `Log Upload Failed` comment gives the reason and the log's location, never a partial log (#1678). Reported upstream as [gh-upload-log#45](https://github.com/link-foundation/gh-upload-log/issues/45) |
| Stop comment: "Review the attached working session log" when nothing was attached | Wording didn't depend on the upload | `logAttached` is passed through; the watch loop attaches before stopping |
| `Skipping: End comment (logs already attached…)` | An earlier iteration's attached log counted | Only the latest attempt counts |
| `solve` exited 0, so Telegram said "finished successfully" | A loop's failed AI session only posted a stop comment | The failure is recorded (`automation-failure.lib.mjs`), and the run exits 1 |
| "✅ finished successfully … recovered from out of memory" | Exit 0 above, plus a child OOM event read as "survived" | With exit 1 the run is resumed. The reply stays **🔄 Work session still in progress** until the recovery session ends |
| `out of memory — 9.8 GB of 11.7 GB RAM available` | Container `OOMKilled` read as exhaustion | Reads "container OOM event — a process in the task cgroup was killed earlier" |
| `Killed-session notice not posted: no-pull-request` | Only issue-started sessions looked a PR up | Falls back to the PR the session was started on |
| A recovery session would replace `📊 Session: 8ed87a4c-…` | The recovery session is tracked under its own id | The reply keeps the root session id and total duration and adds `🔁 Recovery session`. An in-place resume keeps the execution UUID and its single log |
| 1474 × `⚠️ Formatting error detected` | `message is not modified` and other non-formatting 400s were retried as plain text; `/queue` URLs with `_` opened an italic entity | Those are rethrown unchanged, and links render as `[owner/repo#N](url)`. The safety net stays for genuine formatting errors |

Tests (each fails on `main`): `tests/issue-2301-log-upload-resilience.test.mjs`, `tests/issue-2301-stop-comment-log-truth.test.mjs`, `tests/issue-2301-loop-failure-exit.test.mjs`, `tests/issue-2301-oom-resume-in-progress.test.mjs` (monitor replay of the PR-started OOM session: PR notice, 🔄 headline, root id, final ✅ edit), `tests/issue-2301-telegram-formatting-fallbacks.test.mjs`.

## Reproduction and verification

- `experiments/issue-2301-print-bg-ceiling/repro-ceiling.sh` runs live in about two minutes with Claude Code 2.1.284. Its captures are committed. It shows:
  - an 8 s ceiling killing a background agent (`success`, exit 0);
  - the Bash-only exit;
  - a raised ceiling that lets the same agent finish;
  - a same-session `--resume` with the prompt `solve` builds, whose turn reads the partial output, redoes the work in the foreground, and ends with `DONE`.
- `node experiments/issue-2301-print-bg-ceiling/replay-before-after.mjs`: the parser on `main` fails all three real fixtures with `Final tool result failed: The user doesn't want to proceed…`, while this branch schedules a continuation (10, 11 and 4 cancelled tasks).
- `tests/issue-2301-print-bg-ceiling.test.mjs` replays the three real sweeps and the three live captures. It covers:
  - the prompt content and the cap on the task list;
  - the attempt cap (the 5th resume still runs, then it stops);
  - the environment (background work on, ceiling 2400000 ms);
  - the Bash-only exit, `TaskStop`, a later main-thread turn and the stderr pattern.
- `tests/issue-2301-claude-execution.test.mjs` checks the same-session `--resume` through the real command wrapper. `tests/issue-2301-incomplete-claude-turn.test.mjs` checks the attempt cap, OOM classification and relaunch, the truthful notices and the memory limit.
- Local checks:
  - `npm test`: all 520 selected test files pass.
  - `npm run lint`, `npm run format:check`, `npm run check:duplication`, `npm run check:secrets`, `bash scripts/check-file-line-limits.sh`, `bash scripts/check-mjs-syntax.sh`, `GITHUB_BASE_REF=main node scripts/validate-changeset.mjs`.

No UI changes or screenshots are involved.

## CI follow-up

The first run on the implementation head failed the [dependency freshness gate](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/36216047631) with seven stale declarations. This PR now pins secretlint 13.0.6, use-m 8.16.4, command-stream 1.1.0, and links-notation 0.21.3, with matching lockfile and test expectations. The freshness check reports 148/148 current declarations. A live shell quoting regression and CLI smoke checks pass with the refreshed runtime packages.

A later run ([36534908254](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/36534908254)) failed the same gate after nine upstream releases. The pins are refreshed to:

- `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.6
- `start-command` 0.34.1
- `@sentry/node` and `@sentry/profiling-node` 11.1.0; `@sentry/bundler-plugins` 11.1.0 drops its `@babel/core` tree, which removes 31 lockfile entries
- `jscpd` 5.3.3
- `command-stream` 1.2.0
- `links-notation` 0.22.0

The freshness check now reports 151/151. The dependency, use-m and quoting tests, the duplication gate, and the `solve`/`hive --help` smoke runs pass with the new versions.

The latest run failed the gate once more after `command-stream` 1.3.0 was released. It is now pinned as a use-m version, the freshness check reports 151/151, and `experiments/command-stream-1.3.0-smoke.mjs` confirms it loads and quotes arguments correctly.

Run [36623926964](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/actions/runs/36623926964) failed the gate after `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.8 (a dependency refresh) was released. Both Dockerfiles now pin 0.26.8, and the freshness check reports 151/151.

CodeQL flagged two lines. The `/queue` escape helper not escaping `\` is a false positive: legacy Markdown only treats `\` as an escape before `_`, `*`, `` ` `` and `[`, so escaping it would show backslashes doubled. `experiments/issue-2301-codeql/backslash-escaping.mjs` demonstrates this, and a test pins it. The PR-notice test now asserts the exact `gh` arguments.

The first local full-suite run exposed an unrelated race in the existing issue #1823 process-group signal test: under load, it could signal its child before the child installed a SIGINT handler. The test now waits for the child's ready message; the case passed five consecutive isolated runs and a loaded full-suite run.

## Single consolidated remaining-delivery checklist — 2026-09-30

**PR #196 is still incomplete. Complete all remaining implementation, verification and delivery in this PR. Scope is the entire repository. All necessary implementation work is already authorized: do not ask for another maintainer approval, wait for feedback, split away unfinished scope, or treat documented limitations as delivery.**

This is a **new comment**, consolidating the remaining work from [issue #195](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/issues/195), the [full acceptance requirements](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5798732287), the [full-scope authorization](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5802299918), the [delivery correction](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5819788893), the [cleanup requirements](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5856764580), and the [repository-wide grammar/merge/vision directive](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5885245090). Their full obligations remain binding. Earlier permission-to-defer wording does not apply.

### Verified current baseline

Audited branch head: [`01cf1a9389eaf39c08f4383ecb80f1eb3a072052`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/commit/01cf1a9389eaf39c08f4383ecb80f1eb3a072052).

The [latest completed acceptance run](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36598315808), using merge candidate `9e66106f8fbebd8a39ff53c15b3fa64e605675e1`, reports:

- **236/262 pre-merge requirements passing; 26 failing.**
- **604/654 verification cells passing; 50 failing; 0 gate errors.**
- The full manifest contains **266 requirements**: the other **four published-delivery requirements are not discharged by this pre-merge run**.

I inspected the [actual report artifact](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36598315808/artifacts/11047999760), current source/manifest and failed CI logs. This is newer evidence than the 226/262 run quoted in the PR body.

The vision document, hashed source register, traceability, Links Notation 0.22 integration/regressions, naming records/checks, foundation-model/concept-distinction infrastructure, dependency inventory, consumer matrix and grammar-cache cleanup now exist and have passing registered coverage. **Do not recreate those as if absent. Finish their integration and the gaps below.** Passing their present fixtures does not certify all future grammar/semantic workloads.

### 1. Deliver the native grammar system and complete default representations

- [ ] Ship **one common language, recursively represented as links and serialized in Links Notation**, for grammars, concepts, default concrete syntax trees, optional abstract syntax trees, semantic structures and transformations. Make the common links representation operational, not a parallel annotation table around unrelated parsers.
- [ ] Complete the language/version/edition/dialect/alias/extension/embedded-language catalog against every dispatcher, advertised capability and consumer. Inventory applicable official grammars/specifications, ANTLR grammars-v4, tree-sitter and other mature grammars with pinned revisions, licenses, provenance and independent corpora. All existing-language coverage remains the requirement; popular languages and the current catalog are minimum inventories, not a scope cap.
- [ ] Implement the complete grammar feature union in the native representation **and executor**: ordered/unordered alternatives, left and mutual recursion, precedence/associativity, ambiguity/conflicts, lexical priority and longest match, Unicode/byte classes, token/trivia boundaries, lexer modes/channels/state, indentation/layout, contextual predicates, semantic actions/attributes, captures/fields/aliases, parameterization, imports/inheritance, macros/notation, embedded languages and error/missing-node recovery. Scanner and action behavior must be structured executable links, not opaque code strings or hidden language-specific host callbacks.
- [ ] Replace the production tree-sitter/web-tree-sitter/Peggy and foreign parser/scanner routes with the native merged grammars. The current [JavaScript package](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/01cf1a9389eaf39c08f4383ecb80f1eb3a072052/js/package.json) still depends on `peggy` and `web-tree-sitter`; Rust/published packages retain external grammars. Independent external implementations belong in development/test oracles, not the shipped language implementation.
- [ ] Default installed parsing must work offline on first use, without external grammar engines, foreign generated parsers, subprocesses, grammar downloads or caller registration. Generated acceleration is acceptable only when reproducibly derived from the native Links Notation definitions. Test the installed packages with external engines/oracle assets absent, and demonstrate that changing a linked grammar rule changes the **public parse path** without patching host code.
- [ ] For every required language/path, produce complete lossless concrete syntax trees with kinds, fields, hierarchy/order, exact tokens/trivia/source bytes, spans, errors/missing nodes and embedded boundaries. Optional abstract syntax trees must preserve their relation to concrete syntax. Verify query, insert, delete, replace, move, clone and fresh construction; serialization/reload without the original source; edits with updated spans/provenance/diagnostics; and generation/reparse into the intended structure. Text envelopes, token collections and replaying unchanged saved source are not substitutes.
- [ ] Include built-in formats and grammar-description languages in the audit; do not exempt a host-coded parser merely by calling it “native.”

### 2. Finish complete grammar import, conversion, reverse conversion and round trips

- [ ] Deliver matching public APIs and command-line tools in JavaScript and Rust for import, validation, conversion, merging, renaming, export and round-trip checking.
- [ ] Cover all inventoried popular formats, including BNF/EBNF/ABNF, PEG/Peggy/Pest, ANTLR, tree-sitter source and JSON, Lark, GBNF, Yacc/Bison and lexer specifications. Follow included grammars, lexer/scanner definitions and action code. Every format feature needs a native representation, executable meaning and positive/negative tests; rule-skeleton import alone is incomplete.
- [ ] Preserve original names, comments/trivia, source locations, formatting provenance and unique semantics. Imported material must become the inspectable native Links Notation representation, not a foreign parser embedded inside it.
- [ ] Implement conversion back to **every** source format and the full cycle: source grammar → native links → exported grammar → native links. With the original source unavailable to the emitter, test structural/semantic equivalence modulo reversible naming/provenance mappings; test exact reconstruction separately in lossless mode.
- [ ] Execute cross-format and native → external → native cycles under the real independent target tools. Check valid/invalid programs, tree structure, lexical decisions, precedence, actions and recovery/diagnostics. Mutate grammars before export and test malformed cases so returning saved input or two mutually wrong converters cannot pass.
- [ ] For a less expressive target notation, implement faithful lowering/runtime encodings and explicit reconstruction metadata. Distinguish a functioning target grammar from a lossless interchange container. An opaque sidecar, approximation, unsupported diagnostic or syntactically valid output is not completed semantic conversion.

### 3. Finish fully automatic multi-source merging, semantic deduplication and readable naming

- [ ] Implement the non-interactive default pipeline: discover/import all applicable inventoried sources, recognize same-meaning concepts under different names, reconcile definitions, normalize names, deduplicate genuine equivalents, retain unique concepts, and emit a native grammar with a reproducible provenance/decision report.
- [ ] Make **both shipped grammars and native grammars used in tests** outputs of careful multi-source merging. Preserve all compatible sources' unique valid coverage, with explicit edition/dialect boundaries. Do not select a convenient single grammar, merely concatenate rules, namespace every duplicate, indiscriminately union dialects, or derive independent expected results from the merged implementation.
- [ ] Implement binding-aware concept/rule renaming throughout references, imports, captures, actions, mappings and generated artifacts. Keep stable identities and original aliases for export. Test collisions, shadowing, recursion/mutual recursion, qualified references and references after reload.
- [ ] Use meaning-aware normalization, recursive graph/alpha-equivalence, lexical/parser semantics and justified equivalence mappings. Name similarity and finite examples may find candidates but cannot prove arbitrary equivalence. Test differently named equivalents and same-named non-equivalents, including distinct choice, precedence, integer/overflow, binding, effect and universe semantics.
- [ ] Preserve uncertain distinctions and explicit alternatives rather than guessing or discarding information. Resolve the required registered equivalence cases with evidence; unresolved cases remain failing implementation work, not a reason to request maintainer input or permanently require manual mappings.
- [ ] Test deterministic output, idempotence, stability under source reordering, incremental re-merging, collision/conflict resolution and no duplicate canonical identities for established equivalences. Justify source precedence from specifications and independent evidence.
- [ ] Integrate the existing English naming system into the **real importer/merge/export path**. Canonical concepts use unabbreviated English noun phrases; operations/relations use verb phrases. Keep definitions, constraints, stable identities and source aliases. Extend vocabulary, phrase-role, abbreviation, ambiguity and duplicate tests to every generated/merged concept while preserving original language tokens and round trips. Passing the current naming catalog is not evidence that an unimplemented merger names its output correctly.
- [ ] Publish quality comparisons against every inventoried source: construct correctness/coverage, unique-feature preservation and shared-concept reuse, recovery, runtime and memory. “Best possible” needs measured evidence, not a claim based on self-generated fixtures.

### 4. Finish full four-language semantics, transformation and all translations

- [ ] Complete the construct/version/project inventory for **JavaScript, Rust, Lean and Rocq/Coq** and implement each entry through the common editable links representation. Cover full syntax and standard/runtime semantics, not only the portable core.
- [ ] In particular, finish JavaScript classes/objects, array mutation/printing/join, normal imports/modules, Number/BigInt conversions, strings/JSON/remaining standard-library operations, higher-order functions and full asynchronous behavior; and Rust ownership/lifetimes/macros, Lean/Rocq notation, universes, proofs/tactics and all other inventoried facilities. These examples are not the complete scope.
- [ ] Implement project-wide scope/binding/type/universe/effect analysis, module/dependency context, macro/notation expansion and hygiene, proof/tactic elaboration and surface-to-elaborated mappings. Valid supplied context must enable the feature; spelling replacement, roles/spans alone and unavailable capability labels cannot satisfy it. Verify capture avoidance and unaffected comments/strings/regular expressions across nested scopes, imports and proof binders.
- [ ] Complete **all 12 directed pairs in both runtime packages**: JavaScript → Rust/Lean/Rocq; Rust → JavaScript/Lean/Rocq; Lean → JavaScript/Rust/Rocq; Rocq → JavaScript/Rust/Lean. Exercise public parse → links → transform → translate/emit after edits and reload, not a separate string-to-string path disconnected from the representation.
- [ ] Preserve behavior, errors, aborts, overflow, effects and source mappings with faithful target encodings/runtimes where needed. The current [shared emitter](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/01cf1a9389eaf39c08f4383ecb80f1eb3a072052/js/src/translation/emit-common.js#L10) still restricts agreement to non-aborting executions and in-bounds array reads; JavaScript out-of-bounds `undefined` versus a target abort is unfinished fidelity.
- [ ] Preserve theorem/proof meaning with explicit discharged translation obligations, not bounded samples, silently added axioms, weakened statements or checking only the source theorem. Validate target artifacts with the declared hosts/compilers/provers, but do not confuse compiler acceptance with semantic preservation or external kernels with RML's own proof authority.
- [ ] Use the new shared concept/foundation-model infrastructure throughout these paths. Keep genuinely equivalent concepts reusable while retaining different effects, universes and operational models; keep RML syntax/foundation selection/execution/proof policy downstream.

### 5. Complete dependency upgrades; an inventory plus reasons is not the requested update

The [current dependency audit](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/01cf1a9389eaf39c08f4383ecb80f1eb3a072052/docs/dependency-audit.md) explicitly records **46 retained items behind their current stable releases**. The [check](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/01cf1a9389eaf39c08f4383ecb80f1eb3a072052/js/scripts/dependency-inventory.mjs#L602) accepts a behind item when it has a non-placeholder compatibility reason. Accordingly, a green `I195-DEPENDENCY-INVENTORY` is not evidence that the earlier **update-all-dependencies** requirement has been delivered.

- [ ] Resolve the retained outdated runtime/dev/build/optional/transitive dependencies, tools, generators, images, actions and version-coupled artifacts. Upgrade/migrate parent dependencies, implement tested compatibility fixes, or remove obsolete components; do not blindly force incompatible versions.
- [ ] Address the documented Rocq/OCaml/toolchain and build-image constraints with a reproducible supported solution. Removing external production engines should also remove their obsolete build baggage. “Held by another dependency” explains work to do; it does not complete the upgrade.
- [ ] Preserve and rerun Links Notation 0.22 compatibility and upstream regressions in both runtimes and installed artifacts: identity/references/recursion/arity/order, indentation/multiline groups, quoting, comments/trivia/Unicode, exact reconstruction/editability, stack safety and scaling. Verify new native grammar/merge structures too, not just the existing small matrix.
- [ ] Keep a separate failing delivery obligation for unresolved upgrades, even if inventory integrity passes. Refresh registry evidence at the recorded audit date and make the final gate reject stale delivered dependencies rather than converting explanations into acceptance waivers.

issue.title: Large log upload fails on a single transient push error (HTTP 408); retry and push per chunk

repository.name: gh-upload-log
repository.description: A tool to upload the log to GitHub

issue.body:
## Problem

Uploading a large log (165 MB → 2 chunks of ≤100 MB) to the shared `public-logs` repository failed on the only push attempt:

```
Strategy: File exceeds Gist limit, will be split into 2 chunks
→ Adding and committing files...
error: RPC failed; HTTP 408 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 408
send-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet
fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly
❌ Error: Failed to push shared repository upload to public-logs: error: RPC failed; HTTP 408 curl 22 The requested URL returned error: 408
```

In 0.9.2 all chunks are committed together and pushed once (`src/repository-upload.js`, `git push -q -u origin ${defaultBranch}` wrapped by `ensureCommandSucceeded`). A transient 408/5xx or a dropped connection on that single push fails the whole upload.

Observed in https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196 (a hive-mind session log); analysis in https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/pull/2302 (`docs/case-studies/issue-2301`).

## Suggested fixes

1. Retry the push with backoff on transient failures (HTTP 408/429/5xx, `RPC failed`, `the remote end hung up`, `unexpected disconnect`). A `git fetch` + rebase before retrying keeps concurrent uploads to the shared repository working.
2. Push each chunk in its own commit/push, so one request never carries 100+ MB and a retry resends only the failed chunk.
3. Make the chunk size configurable (for example `--chunk-size 50MB`) for slow or proxied connections.
4. Split chunks on line boundaries (and never inside a multi-byte UTF-8 character), so every part is independently readable.

## Workaround in hive-mind

hive-mind now retries the whole upload three times with backoff and then re-uploads the log itself as complete line-aligned parts (`src/log-upload.lib.mjs` in link-assistant/hive-mind#2302). If that also fails, it posts a comment on the pull request saying that the log is missing, and why.

## What remains after the latest changes — audit of PR head `7489adfb`

**Finish issue #195 and the complete repository-wide vision in this PR.** Implementation and verification are already authorized. [The prior consolidated directive](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5895896874) and all registered requirement-bearing comments remain in force; this is the updated remaining-work list, not a reduction of scope.

The current [manifest](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/7489adfb34f9b882b9b086a8c279d3b3cb77028c/parity/issue-195-requirements.json) has **270 atomic requirements**. The [latest full acceptance run](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36626831406) evaluated this head as merge candidate `b6bc6754`: **236/266 pre-merge requirements pass, 30 fail; 604/659 verification cells pass, 55 fail; zero gate errors**. [The report artifact](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/36626831406/artifacts/11061706472) shows missing implementation entry points and missing observed execution for all 30 failing rows. Four additional published-delivery rows remain pending.

Progress since the previous comment is real: Rust lint and standard package CI now pass; grammar documentation points to this PR; Links Notation 0.22 and its regressions, the committed vision/source register, naming checks, and cache cleanup are present; a packed JavaScript candidate passed **1,506 RML PR #184 tests** after the rendering fix; and [repository rule 24204187](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/rules/24204187) now requires the Full Requirements Aggregate. Preserve these results and finish what follows.

### Exact rows still without implementation or executed acceptance evidence

| Work | Requirement IDs |
| --- | --- |
| Native grammars and lossless CSTs | `I195-GRAMMAR-DEPENDENCY-BOUNDARY`, `I195-GRAMMAR-FEATURE-UNION`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LANGUAGE-CATALOG`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LOSSLESS-TREES`, `I195-GRAMMAR-NATIVE-MERGED` |
| Import, export and round trips | `I195-INTERCHANGE-API-CLI`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-CROSS-FORMAT-TOOLS`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-FAITHFUL-LOWERING`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-FORMAT-FEATURES`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-MUTATION-GUARDS`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-REVERSE-CONVERSION` |
| Automatic grammar merging | `I195-MERGE-AUTOMATIC-PIPELINE`, `I195-MERGE-BINDING-AWARE-RENAME`, `I195-MERGE-DETERMINISM`, `I195-MERGE-MEANING-AWARE-DEDUPLICATION`, `I195-MERGE-QUALITY-EVIDENCE`, `I195-MERGE-SHIPPED-GRAMMARS-ARE-MERGED`, `I195-MERGE-UNCERTAINTY-PRESERVED` |
| Four-language semantics and proofs | `I195-SEMANTICS-CONSTRUCT-INVENTORY`, `I195-SEMANTICS-FAITHFUL-BEHAVIOR`, `I195-SEMANTICS-PROOF-PRESERVATION` |
| Dependencies and parser removal | `I195-DEPENDENCY-CURRENT-STABLE-DELIVERY`, `I195-DEPENDENCY-PRODUCTION-PARSERS-REMOVED` |
| RML, formal-ai and TypeScript | `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-WORKLOADS`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-RML-PR184-AUDIT`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-RML-WORKLOADS`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-TYPESCRIPT-TRANSLATIONS` |
| Acceptance and merge enforcement | `I195-ACCEPTANCE-GATE-MUTATIONS`, `I195-ACCEPTANCE-INDEPENDENT-ORACLES`, `I195-ACCEPTANCE-REQUIRED-MERGE-CHECK` |

The table includes `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-PUBLISHED`, which is a release-stage row. The 30 other IDs are the exact failing pre-merge rows in the current report. A declared entry point, a planned fixture or a broad green test must not stand in for the missing behavior and observed assertions.

### Required implementation

1. **Native grammars and default trees.** Expand the linked grammar representation and executor to the complete inventoried feature union: recursion and precedence, lexical modes/state and scanner actions, context-sensitive constructs, layout, embeddings, notation and error recovery. Carefully merge pinned official, ANTLR, tree-sitter and other mature sources into **native Links Notation grammars** for every required language, edition, dialect and alias. Run those native definitions through the installed public parser in both runtimes without external grammar engines, foreign generated parsers, downloads or caller registration. Remove production `peggy`, `web-tree-sitter`, tree-sitter crates and vendored parser binaries once replaced; retain independent external parsers as test oracles. Verify changing a linked rule changes the public parse result. Produce complete lossless CSTs by default, optional ASTs with provenance, and source-free edit/reload/emit/reparse evidence. All existing-language coverage remains the target; today's catalog is a minimum audit.

2. **Grammar interchange.** Finish public JavaScript/Rust APIs and CLI tools that import, validate, convert, merge, rename and export BNF/EBNF/ABNF, PEG/Peggy/Pest, ANTLR, tree-sitter source/JSON, Lark, GBNF, Yacc/Bison, lexer specifications and other inventoried formats. Represent their actual lexical, scanner and action semantics as executable links. Convert **back** to every format after discarding original input; test source → links → export → links, native → external → native and cross-format cycles with independent target tools. Compare accepted/rejected inputs, syntax structures, precedence, actions and diagnostics. Mutate before export and test malformed grammars to catch saved-input replay and mutually wrong converters. Faithful target encodings must preserve unique features and reversible provenance; lossy approximations are unfinished.

3. **Automatic multi-source merging.** Build the non-interactive pipeline that discovers all applicable sources, recognizes same-meaning concepts with different names, merges them without collapsing distinct meanings, and emits deterministic canonical grammars plus a reproducible decision report. Both production and native test grammars must be merge outputs. Implement binding-aware concept renaming across references, imports, captures, actions and generated artifacts; preserve original aliases for reverse conversion. Test collisions, shadowing, recursion, idempotence, input reordering, incremental updates and edition boundaries. Use semantic evidence for equivalence, preserve uncertain alternatives, apply the already delivered unabbreviated English noun/verb naming rules to **generated** concepts, and compare coverage/correctness/recovery/performance against the independent sources.

4. **Full language semantics and translation.** Complete project-wide structured representation, binding/type/universe/effect elaboration, hygiene, construction and transformations for **JavaScript, Rust, Lean and Rocq/Coq**. Include ordinary classes/objects/imports, mutable arrays, strings/JSON/conversions, standard behavior, Rust ownership/macros and Lean/Rocq notation/proofs/tactics, along with every other inventoried construct. Complete **all 12 directed translations in both runtime packages** through the editable common links. Preserve errors, aborts, overflow, effects, source mappings and proof meaning through faithful target encodings and discharged obligations. [Current emitter assumptions](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/7489adfb34f9b882b9b086a8c279d3b3cb77028c/js/src/translation/emit-common.js#L10) still restrict agreement to non-aborting executions and in-bounds array reads. Bounded checks and target compilation alone do not prove theorem preservation. Keep RML-specific foundations and proof authority in RML.

5. **Dependencies and downstream work.** [The dependency audit](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/7489adfb34f9b882b9b086a8c279d3b3cb77028c/docs/dependency-audit.md#L627) still lists **46 retained items behind** their recorded current releases. Solve parent constraints, update or replace outdated retained components, and make the delivery gate reject stale dependencies; a recorded reason is not an upgrade. Complete RML PR #184's actual parse → links → transform/translate → emit integration in **both** runtime packages, including Rust candidate and clean published consumers. The PR #184 audit text and 1,506 passing JavaScript candidate tests are useful progress; `I195-DOWNSTREAM-RML-PR184-AUDIT` still needs its real implementation entry and observed assertions. Exercise formal-ai's own fixtures and rules in clean installed consumers, including required Rust/JavaScript/TypeScript projection translations; a TypeScript CST alone does not satisfy that workload.

6. **Acceptance and publication.** Run native merged grammars against pinned independent ANTLR/tree-sitter/official corpora and representative real projects in both runtimes. Add positive/negative, property/fuzz/metamorphic, Unicode, malformed, embedded, edit-sequence and gate-mutation tests with observed assertions and reproducers. Prove the gate rejects native parser bypass, broken reverse conversion, semantic duplicates, abbreviated names, stale dependencies, missing source requirements, weakened oracles, unsupported translation and bounded-proof substitutes. The live merge rule is now active, so wire `I195-ACCEPTANCE-REQUIRED-MERGE-CHECK` to **observed live rule evidence** rather than recreating the rule. Complete published `I195-DELIVERY-CRATE-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-NPM-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-RML-PUBLISHED` and `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-PUBLISHED`: npm still serves `meta-language@0.46.0` while branch source is 0.58.2. Verify exact published npm/crate artifacts, checksums, offline-first public APIs and real RML/formal-ai workload results.

Register this **new comment** in `parity/issue-195-sources.json` and reconcile the atomic ledger. Run the full gate on the final head and merge candidate, then update the PR body: it currently says “Draft” while GitHub reports `isDraft: false`. The [latest automated session](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5898232595) stopped on expired Codex authentication; restore its access and continue. That operational failure does not alter any delivery requirement.

**Completion is all 266 pre-merge rows and four publication rows passing with the full original scope represented, real implementation and independent evidence. No additional maintainer scope decision or approval is needed.**

feat: thread aborts as values through Lean and Rocq targets

A machine-integer operation, a checked conversion and an explicit abort
now test where the source aborts and return the source's message in the
generated ml_io pair; main stops there, printing the lines before it, so
Lean throws the message and Rocq's main is the lines with Some message.
The non-aborting assumption is gone.

feat: the foundation models encode aborts and machine integers instead of assuming them

Overflow and the abort of a total target become encodings (machine-integer,
abort-threading), so no conformance pair carries an assumption. An assertion's
first operand that prints or aborts now runs before it, as it does in the
source, and Lean evaluates main's runs before deciding the assertion.
test: a corpus of programs that abort, overflow, divide by zero or print from a function, with the source run's lines and abort

test: run every faithful-corpus program and its 12 directed translations and compare lines and aborts

The faithful corpus moves into four-language-conformance.json as faithfulBehavior,
gains a BigInt program past 64 bits, and a JavaScript test observes each
source and translation with its own toolchain, including a fault-injected abort.
test: the Rust twin of the faithful-behavior test, and the requirement row's entry points

feat: audit the current relative-meta-logic pull request 184 head and every file of it that reaches meta-language

The fixture pins the head and inventories its workloads by following imports
from the package; the audit section links each at that head and maps it to
ledger rows with executable acceptance cells; in acceptance mode the test
derives the inventory again from the live pull request on GitHub.

fix: abort-threaded Lean main and assertions parse with the Lean grammar, and generated ml_io pairs are not source mappings

The abort-threaded assertion theorem used `conv => whnf`, which the Lean
grammar does not parse; its statement is now a Bool the kernel evaluates,
proved by rfl or decide. The unwrap of a step is a multi-line match, since a
single-line match followed by another do statement does not parse. A
generated ml_io pair has no source declaration, so it is no longer mapped.

feat: the Rust translator threads aborts and machine integers as the JavaScript one does

Ports output.js abort threading (aborts.rs, output.rs) and the machine-integer
and abort-threading encodings to the Rust pipeline, with the emitters' abort
spellings in every target. Stage parity holds on every recorded program.

chore: install and declare Rocq 9.3.0 now that opam publishes it

rocq-core 9.3.0 was merged into opam-repository (PR 30776). The acceptance
workflow installs it with rocq-stdlib 9.2.0 (which requires rocq-core >= 9.1),
and every declared Rocq toolchain version moves from 9.2 to 9.3. The pinned
stdlib 9.2.0 conformance sources are unchanged.

feat: run the relative-meta-logic pull request 184 workloads on the exact candidate artifacts

A new acceptance job installs the npm tarball from an empty node_modules and
fresh cache into RML's js/, patches RML's rust/ to the unpacked .crate, checks
both resolve to the artifacts, runs RML's own workload tests and the consumer
probes, and uploads a report. The JavaScript and Rust tests validate that
report and observe the four I195-DOWNSTREAM-RML-WORKLOADS assertions.

feat: a native grammar executor runs every feature of the grammar feature union, and peggy becomes a development dependency

The JavaScript package parses grammars with its own executor over the
representation in docs/grammar/feature-union.md. The shared fixture
parity/fixtures/grammar-feature-union.json covers the 17 features of the
vision with 43 positive and 48 negative cases and a grammar mutation per
feature. Peggy stays only as a development dependency and test oracle.
The Rust port has not reached parity yet, so the row stays open.

feat: the JavaScript EBNF importer reports an inline regex as unsupported, as the Rust one does

An EBNF `#'...'` element was a parse error in JavaScript and an unsupported construct in Rust. Both now report it as unsupported. The comments no longer cite the Rust `bnf` and `ebnf` crates, which the Rust importers stop using.

refactor: port the ABNF, BNF, EBNF and pest importers from JavaScript to hand-written Rust

The four importers are now faithful ports of js/src/grammar-importers/{abnf,bnf-ebnf,pest,common}.js, sharing a cursor and rule assembly in import/common.rs. They no longer go through the abnf, bnf, ebnf and pest_meta crates. A differential run over the fixtures, the parity sources, handcrafted edge cases and 40 mutations of each (4674 inputs) gives identical IR and diagnostics, with two exceptions. A lone surrogate numeric value is unsupported in Rust, whose strings cannot hold one. Inverted or overflowing repetition bounds are a parse error in Rust where JavaScript throws a RangeError.

chore: drop the abnf, bnf, ebnf and pest_meta runtime dependencies

pest_meta stays as a dev-dependency for validating emitted .pest grammars. The build pruned 22 packages from Cargo.lock without bumping any remaining one: abnf, abnf-core, bnf, ebnf, foldhash 0.2, getrandom 0.3, hashbrown 0.16, html-escape, minimal-lexical, nom 7, parse-hyperlinks, ppv-lite86, r-efi 5, rand, rand_chacha and rand_core 0.9, thiserror and thiserror-impl 1, wasip2, wit-bindgen 0.57, and zerocopy and zerocopy-derive. The dependency inventory drops those items, records pest_meta as a development dependency, and drops the removed packages from the held reasons of allocator-api2, hashbrown 0.15 and syn. docs/dependency-audit.md is re-rendered from it. Delivery problems go from 43 to 30.
Merge the native Rust ABNF, BNF, EBNF and pest importers

chore: follow Rust 1.99.0, tree-sitter-graphql 0.3.0, tree-sitter-haskell 0.24.1 and yoke-derive 0.8.4

The live dependency check flags each of these releases from the last two
days. The acceptance workflow installs Rust 1.99.0 and every contract,
dependency list and evidence record declares it. The two grammar crates
move to their current releases and the vendored WebAssembly parsers are
rebuilt from the same crates with tree-sitter CLI 0.27.0, so both runtimes
keep identical generated parsers. The inventory is refreshed online, which
also confirms the hand-edited entries of the native importer merge.
test: the acceptance workflow pin test follows Rust 1.99.0 and Rocq 9.3.0

fix: the RML workload runner reads plain cargo output and checks RML items by Rust path

CI exports CARGO_TERM_COLOR=always, so the libtest transcript carried ANSI
styling and no 'Running <file>' line matched: every probe read as not run
although all 44 Rust tests passed. The runner now asks cargo for plain output
and strips styling before parsing.

The 'names no RML item' check matched the upstream name inside provenance
strings of the parity corpus (src/parity.rs, src/parity_fixtures.rs). It now
looks for Rust paths and extern crates, which is what naming an item means.
fix: Rust evidence stays in the Rust tree and tests follow clippy 1.99's assert_is_empty

feat(rust): the grammar model reads and writes the feature union forms and declarations

GrammarExpr gains a Feature variant (FeatureExpr: the feature forms, byte and
Unicode classes, and parameterized calls), GrammarRule gains RuleAttributes and
Grammar gains GrammarDeclarations. The native listing, the normalized JSON
document and the links codec read and write them the way the JavaScript model
does; every consumer of GrammarExpr either handles the new variant or reports
it as unsupported.

feat: the delivery gate accepts only current or verified newest-compatible releases and checks the audit against live registries

Held items now record the newest release every holder admits and the holders
themselves, re-derived from the registries and the Cargo resolve graph. The
delivery check rejects an item unless it is current, or at that compatible
release with every holder inventoried and itself delivered. --live re-queries
the registries and rejects an outdated audit; CI and acceptance runs go live
by default. The audit of 2026-10-02 finds no pin behind its compatible release.
fix: a failed live dependency refresh stops querying the remaining registries

test: observe current-stable delivery on the committed inventory, lockfiles and vendored artifacts

The test reads parity/dependency-inventory.json and the files it describes:
every retained item is current or at its verified newest compatible release,
held lockfile items are held by delivered dependents that the lockfiles show
depending on them, toolchains, actions and images are current or held by
delivered pins, the vendored grammars and runtime match their source pins and
recorded digests, and the gate rejects stale pins, unverified holds, stale
holders and an audit the live registries no longer match.

ci: the clean-consumer acceptance job runs the live dependency delivery gate

The Ubuntu consumer checks the installed lockfile of the packed npm artifact
and compares the recorded audit with the live registries; the requirement
catalog pins the refreshed inventory digest.
docs: newest compatible releases, verified holders and the live delivery gate
Merge the current-stable dependency delivery gate
chore: register the maintainer's merge condition comment as a source (status, no new requirements)
chore: refresh the issue 195 manifest for the registered merge-condition comment

feat(rust): native executor of the grammar feature union with fixture-driven tests

Port js/src/grammar-runtime/ to rust/src/grammar/feature_runtime/: imports,
macros, parameterized rules and embedded languages load; left recursion,
precedence, conflicts, dynamic precedence, longest match, Unicode and byte
classes, extras, immediate tokens, modes, channels, scanners, predicates,
actions, captures, aliases, ERROR/MISSING recovery and resource limits
execute, producing the same trees and tree notation as JavaScript.
rust/tests/unit/issue_195_grammar_feature_union.rs runs every case and
mutation of parity/fixtures/grammar-feature-union.json byte for byte.

feat: run the link-assistant/formal-ai workloads on the exact candidate artifacts

A new acceptance job checks out formal-ai at the pinned revision and verifies
every inventoried blob. It patches formal-ai's rust/ to the unpacked .crate,
first refreshing Cargo.lock for meta-language alone, because the lock pins
tree-sitter-language 0.1.7 and the candidate needs ^0.1.8. It checks that the
build links only the candidate and runs formal-ai's own meta-language test
groups with a probe of formal-ai's Rust functions. formal-ai's npm package
has no meta-language dependency, so a clean consumer of the npm tarball runs
formal-ai's Links Notation data through the public JavaScript API. The two
runtimes' outputs are compared. The JavaScript and Rust suites validate the
report and observe the three I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-WORKLOADS assertions
only when they hold.

fix: grammar merge and lowering carry the feature union declarations and rule fields

Merging (JavaScript and Rust) now renames and keeps the grammar
declarations and the parameters, channel, modes and action of each rule:
rule fields take part in rule signatures and fingerprints, imports, modes,
extras and conflict groups are united, and the first matching, macro or
scanner of a name wins with a different later one reported as a
declaration-conflict decision and alternative.

Lowering records the declarations and rule fields as declarations and
attributes metadata steps (status approximate, since no lowered
executable honors them), reconstructs them, and reports feature-dropped
when they are removed from the metadata.

The interchange section of parity/fixtures/grammar-feature-union.json
records the JavaScript outcome; both runtimes compare against it.

fix: register the grammar.feature-union-form concept record

The Rust grammar model names feature union expressions
grammar.feature-union-form (concept identity) and
grammar::expression::feature-union-form (link term); the naming check
requires a concept record for both. The generated concept records of
both packages are rebuilt from the register.

chore: wire I195-GRAMMAR-FEATURE-UNION to its implementations and fixture

The requirement row names the JavaScript and Rust entry points and pins
parity/fixtures/grammar-feature-union.json, which the JavaScript and Rust
observations now cite; the manifest is refreshed. parity/language-features.json
gains a grammar-feature-union row, docs/grammar/feature-union.md states
the Rust status and the known gaps, and a Rust changelog fragment records
the semver-breaking enum variants.
Merge the Rust port of the grammar feature union
chore: refresh the issue 195 manifest after merging the Rust feature union

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body: Here it is visible, that the task is still in the queue: Yet here instead of showing warnings and how many times it was recovered from OOM we display that it actually failed. Yet at the same time queue shows it is being active: So this message is surely misleading. ## What remains for full delivery — audit of PR head `d2407c18`, 2026-10-02

**PR #196 is not complete, and its CI is red.** The [previous audit](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5906611497), the [consolidated directive](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5895896874) and every registered requirement-bearing comment remain in force. This comment is the updated remaining-work list plus **new mandatory working rules for resource use**. It does not reduce scope. Implementation and verification are already authorized; do not wait for another maintainer response.

### Progress since `7489adfb` (keep it)

The last acceptance run that compiled ([run 37004646383](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/37004646383), merge candidate `cd41314a`) passed **250/266 pre-merge requirements** (was 236/266). These 14 rows moved from FAIL to PASS: `I195-ACCEPTANCE-GATE-MUTATIONS`, `I195-DEPENDENCY-CURRENT-STABLE-DELIVERY`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-RML-PR184-AUDIT`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-RML-WORKLOADS`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-API-CLI`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-FAITHFUL-LOWERING`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-MUTATION-GUARDS`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-REVERSE-CONVERSION`, `I195-MERGE-BINDING-AWARE-RENAME`, `I195-MERGE-DETERMINISM`, `I195-MERGE-MEANING-AWARE-DEDUPLICATION`, `I195-MERGE-UNCERTAINTY-PRESERVED`, `I195-SEMANTICS-FAITHFUL-BEHAVIOR`, `I195-SEMANTICS-PROOF-PRESERVATION`. `peggy` is no longer a production npm dependency. The ABNF/BNF/EBNF/pest importers are now hand-written Rust. Retained dependencies behind current releases dropped from 46 to 28.

### 1. Make CI green first — “Nothing must fail”

Per [the maintainer's merge condition](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5947888429), every check must pass. At `d2407c18`, 10 checks fail:

- **Rust does not compile.** `error[E0004]: non-exhaustive patterns: &GrammarExpr::Feature(_) not covered` at `rust/tests/integration/inference_minimize.rs:89`. The new variant came from the feature-union merge (`26978038`/`d8810804`). This one error fails **Test (ubuntu/macos/windows)**, **Minimum Supported Rust Version**, **Lint and Format Check**, **Code Coverage** and **Fresh Merge Simulation**. It also makes `suite-rust` exit 101 in the acceptance job, so the **Full Requirements Aggregate collapses from 250/266 to 11/266**. Handle the variant there and in every other exhaustive `match` on `GrammarExpr`. Then push only after `cargo check --all-targets --all-features` passes locally.
- **Formal AI Workloads fail in both runtimes.** JavaScript: 137/147. Rust: 129/134 ([run 37014655368](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/37014655368)). These are **meta-language JS↔Rust parity regressions**, not formal-ai defects:
  - The JS runtime rejects formal-ai's `data/seed/grammar-projection-rules.lino`: `S-expression query must start with (node_type) @capture`. Rust loads the same file with 121 rules, 62 refusals and 131 no-form rows.
  - The JS runtime fails on the seed network with `link id must be a positive integer, got meta`.
  - JS `toLino`/`fromLino` keeps **0 named nodes** and fails the round trip on **all 133** formal-ai `.lino` files. Rust keeps 380 named nodes and round-trips.
  - The runtimes differ on 51/121 bound captures, 40/121 root-link matches, 58/121 accepted match S-expressions and 9/12 projections.
  - Rust fails `issue_425` (3 tests: Markdown→HTML routing, lossy Markdown→txt reporting, document formats available) and `issue_673_self_ast_census::committed_census_documents_match_what_the_sources_render`.

  Fix the JavaScript reader, query parser and Links Notation round trip until both runtimes agree on every formal-ai fixture. Add each failing formal-ai input as a **local regression fixture** in `parity/` so it is caught by the fast package tests, not only by the 10-minute workload job.
- **Update the PR description.** It says “this PR stays draft” while GitHub reports `isDraft: false`. The description must state the real status.

### 2. Requirement rows still failing (16 pre-merge + 4 publication)

| Work | Requirement IDs | What is missing |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native grammars and lossless trees | `I195-GRAMMAR-DEPENDENCY-BOUNDARY`, `I195-GRAMMAR-FEATURE-UNION`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LANGUAGE-CATALOG`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LOSSLESS-TREES`, `I195-GRAMMAR-NATIVE-MERGED` | Native Links Notation grammars for every catalog language must be run by the native executor in both runtimes, with no tree-sitter or other foreign parser on the production path. `I195-GRAMMAR-FEATURE-UNION` was wired in `94fa9527` but has never been observed, because Rust does not compile. |
| Interchange | `I195-INTERCHANGE-CROSS-FORMAT-TOOLS`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-FORMAT-FEATURES` | Cross-format cycles checked by independent target tools. Every inventoried format feature (lexer modes, scanner actions, precedence, actions) must be represented and exported. |
| Automatic merging | `I195-MERGE-AUTOMATIC-PIPELINE`, `I195-MERGE-QUALITY-EVIDENCE`, `I195-MERGE-SHIPPED-GRAMMARS-ARE-MERGED` | Every shipped grammar must be the output of the non-interactive multi-source pipeline, with coverage, correctness, recovery and performance compared against the sources. |
| Semantics | `I195-SEMANTICS-CONSTRUCT-INVENTORY` | Implementation entry point and observed assertions for the full JavaScript/Rust/Lean/Rocq construct inventory. |
| Dependencies | `I195-DEPENDENCY-PRODUCTION-PARSERS-REMOVED` | `web-tree-sitter` is still a production npm dependency, and `rust/Cargo.toml` still lists 56 `tree-sitter*` crates. Keep them only as dev-dependency **test oracles** once native grammars replace them. |
| Downstream | `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-WORKLOADS`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-TYPESCRIPT-TRANSLATIONS` | See the formal-ai regressions in section 1. Add the TypeScript projection translations from formal-ai's own fixtures. |
| Acceptance | `I195-ACCEPTANCE-INDEPENDENT-ORACLES`, `I195-ACCEPTANCE-REQUIRED-MERGE-CHECK` | See below for the merge check. |
| Publication (release checkpoint) | `I195-DELIVERY-CRATE-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-NPM-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-RML-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-PUBLISHED` | npm still serves `meta-language@0.46.0`; the branch is `0.58.2`. |

Every row except the merge check fails with *“implementation entry point is not supplied; execution record is missing”*. That is missing implementation, not missing paperwork.

**`I195-ACCEPTANCE-REQUIRED-MERGE-CHECK`:** The live [ruleset 24204187](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/rules/24204187) is active on `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`. It requires `Full Requirements Aggregate` with `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true` and has **no bypass actors**; this was read with an admin token on 2026-10-02. The script nevertheless reports “Full Requirements Aggregate is not a strict required check” and “no active, non-bypassable rule”. That is a **defect in `check-issue-195-merge-enforcement.mjs`**. With the workflow token, read the strict policy from `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/main`, which the workflow token can read. Only the bypass-actor list needs `ISSUE_195_RULESET_TOKEN`. Fix the script so that each assertion fails only on its own missing evidence.

**Stopping is not allowed.** A [previous session](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5946897834) ended with “No code changed this iteration, because none of the 20 open pre-merge rows can be finished in one session.” That is not an acceptable outcome. A row too large for one session is delivered as **a series of committed, pushed, working increments**: for example, one language's native grammar at a time, each with its own tests. Every session must push real progress on an open row.

### 3. Mandatory working rules: resources, batching, cleanup

Automated sessions on this PR keep dying. The [latest one](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5953703216) was killed with **exit code 137** (out of memory) inside the Docker task container after several hours. The [maintainer already asked](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5940086274) for the following; it is now required:

1. **Work in bulk.** Draft a whole batch of related changes, commit, re-read the diff, then commit again. Push once the batch is complete; **CI is the full verifier.** Do not rebuild or re-test the whole project after each edit.
2. **Prefer JavaScript for experiments.** Prototype a grammar, executor, merge or translation change in `js/` first; it needs no compilation. Port the finished design to `rust/` in one batch, then run `cargo check` once.
3. **Run only targeted local checks**, with bounded parallelism:
   - JS: `node --test tests/<area>*.test.js` for the files you touched.
   - Rust: `cargo check --all-targets --all-features`, then `cargo test --test integration <filter>` or `--test unit <filter>`, with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2`, `RUST_TEST_THREADS=2` and `CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`.
   - **Never run locally:** the full `acceptance:issue-195` pipeline, `run-issue-195-evidence.mjs`, the native Lean/Rocq/Rust toolchain matrix, clean-consumer installs, the RML/formal-ai workload clones, `cargo llvm-cov`, or upstream-corpus and whole-registry experiments. Those belong to CI.
4. **Fix `AGENTS.md`.** It currently says “Run the JavaScript checks (`npm test && npm run check`) and the Rust checks (… `cargo test --all-features`) before pushing.” That contradicts rule 3. Replace it with the targeted-check rule and a pointer to the CI jobs that do the full verification.
5. **Always be ready to clean up.** Run `node scripts/clean-caches.mjs` after every batch and before any long command. Remove `.issue-195-work/`, `issue-195-results/`, `issue-195-artifacts/`, cloned RML/formal-ai checkouts and their `target/` directories once a step is done. On a timeout or failure, kill leftover `cargo`, `rustc`, `node`, `lean`, `lake`, `coqc` and `rocq` processes before continuing. Commit early so an OOM kill loses nothing.

### 4. Split CI so a single failure is reported in minutes, not after the whole pipeline

Today one compile error costs 7 Rust jobs and a ~20-minute acceptance job, and it reports 255 false row failures. Change the workflows as follows, without weakening or removing any check:

- **Add a fast `cargo check --all-targets --all-features` gate (about 2 minutes).** Make Test, MSRV, Coverage, Fresh Merge and acceptance `needs:` it, so a compile error fails once, early.
- **Split test execution by category** into matrix jobs with their own 10–15-minute timeouts: Rust by target and filter (`--test unit`, and `--test integration` split into `grammar_*`, `inference_*`, and translation/conformance), and JS `node --test` by file group (grammar, translation, conformance/generative, downstream, tooling). Keep the existing check names, or add an aggregating job with the same name, so the required ruleset context stays valid.
- **Split the “Produce checkpoint evidence” step.** Today `run-issue-195-evidence.mjs` runs `suite-javascript`, `suite-rust`, every native translation pair for both runtimes, delivery packing and merge enforcement **sequentially in one step**, and it installs Lean, OCaml and Rocq even when Rust cannot build. Make these separate jobs: JS suite, Rust suite, native translations as a matrix by target language, delivery, merge enforcement. Each job uploads its own evidence artifact, and `Full Requirements Aggregate` only merges and evaluates them. If a suite cannot build, report it as **one gate error naming the suite**, not as 255 failing rows.
- **Add `concurrency: { group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}, cancel-in-progress: true }`** to every workflow. Head `8418ce50` alone started seven Issue 195 Full Acceptance runs.
- **Shrink the runtime-parity evidence.** The requirement report artifact is about 208 MB, and 188 MB of it is two 94 MB files: `issue-195-results/runtime-parity/{javascript,rust}.json`. Each holds the **complete serialized CST of every fixture**: 308 PDF-grammar trees of about 108 KB each (76 MB), 655 Links Notation grammar trees (12 MB) and 80 inventory trees (8 MB). `js/scripts/check-issue-195-runtime-parity.mjs` captures the Rust document through `execFileSync` with `maxBuffer: 512 * 1024 * 1024`, then runs `JSON.parse` on it. It also builds the JavaScript document in the same process and `stableJson`-stringifies both. That puts several copies of roughly 100 MB of trees in one Node heap at once. Record a stable digest per fixture and compare the digests; write the full trees **only for fixtures whose digests differ**. Stream results per fixture (for example, NDJSON) instead of building one giant string.

### 5. Memory and bottleneck audit of the code

A static review of `d2407c18` found no unbounded growth in the Rust `OnceLock` tables or the executor memo, which is capped by `memoLimit`. It did find these **unreasonable resource costs**. Fix each one and add a regression check where it can be measured, for example a bounded `--max-old-space-size` run or a peak-RSS assertion in CI.

1. **Uncapped parallel compile and test inside the evidence runner.** `js/scripts/run-issue-195-evidence.mjs:234-239` starts `npm test` **and** `cargo test --all-features` at the same time, in one `Promise.all`. `runCommand` (`:720`) passes `process.env` through unchanged, so there is no `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` or `RUST_TEST_THREADS` limit. `scripts/with-cache-cleanup.mjs` already sets those bounds, but this path does not use it. `--all-features` also compiles `lindera` with the embedded Jieba dictionary and `doublets`, on top of 57 `tree-sitter*` crates and 5 C grammars from `build.rs`. This is the most likely cause of the exit-137 kills, because agents follow `AGENTS.md` and run this locally. Run the suites sequentially, apply the bounded environment to every child process, and only enable the features that a requirement actually needs.
2. **All 60 WebAssembly grammars load eagerly at import time and are never freed.** `js/src/programming-language-parser.js:32-41` decompresses all 60 grammars and calls `Language.load` for each one in a module-level `Map` before anything is parsed. That is 7.6 MB of gzip, several times larger once decompressed, in the WASM heap of every process that imports the parser, including every `node --test` file process. Load each grammar on first use and cache it by ID.
3. **A new parser for every Markdown inline node.** `programming-language-parser.js:359` creates and deletes a `WebTreeSitterParser` for every `inline` or `pipe_table_cell` node. That means hundreds of WASM allocations for each large document. Reuse one parser, and still delete each tree.
4. **Per-character offset maps for every parse.** `sourceBoundaries` (`programming-language-parser.js:467-486`) builds a `Map` entry for **every character**, and `clipParsedSource` calls it twice (`:86`, `:118`). `utf8Input` (`:156-173`) keeps the text, its UTF-8 bytes and a complete UTF-16 byte string at the same time. On large Lean, Rocq or registry sources this is several times the input size per parse. Use sorted line or chunk checkpoints with binary search, and decode bytes in the `read` callback as they are needed.
5. **The runtime-parity evidence serializes everything** (see section 4): about 94 MB per runtime, read through a 512 MB `maxBuffer` and parsed in one heap. Switch to per-fixture digests and full trees only for fixtures that differ.
6. **Cache cleanup only runs on commit and in CI teardown.** `scripts/clean-caches.mjs` runs from the pre-commit hook, the opt-in `with-cache-cleanup.mjs` wrapper and the CI teardown. A long agent session that builds without committing never triggers it. Make `with-cache-cleanup.mjs` the documented way to run every local cargo or npm test command, and run it between batches.
7. **Native validation output stays on disk for the rest of the acceptance job.** `.rmeta`, `.olean` and `.vo` outputs under `issue-195-results/work/native/` remain until the final teardown, and some are uploaded. Delete them once each native cell is recorded.

### Completion condition

All checks on the final head are green, including the 10 failing now. All 266 pre-merge rows and the 4 publication rows pass with real implementation and independent observed evidence. The workflow split and resource rules above are delivered. The memory issues in section 5 are fixed, with regression tests that bound memory use. Register **this comment** in `parity/issue-195-sources.json` and reconcile the ledger: add atomic rows for the CI split, the `AGENTS.md` resource rules and each memory fix in section 5, without removing or weakening any existing row.

message: fix: cover GrammarExpr::Feature in the inference minimize test helper

fix(js): match the Rust formal-ai query, LiNo and projection outputs

Port the Rust query matcher to js/src/query.js, write and read the canonical
Links Notation form in js/src/lino-serialization.js, store syntax fields as
Rust's [parent, label, child] Field links, and run formal-ai's own projection
walk in the JavaScript probe. The formal-ai inputs that disagreed are kept in
parity/fixtures/formal-ai-regressions/ with a Rust golden that
js/tests/issue-195-formal-ai-regressions.test.js compares against.

docs: targeted local checks and resource limits for agents and contributors

AGENTS.md and CONTRIBUTING.md now list the per-area JavaScript and Rust
commands to run locally, the CARGO_BUILD_JOBS/RUST_TEST_THREADS/CARGO_INCREMENTAL
limits, the suites that run only in CI, and the batch cleanup steps.

fix: keep the published cross-format concept identities resolving

formal-ai's issue_425 tests list and match CROSS_FORMAT_CONCEPTS as published
(`strong`). CROSS_FORMAT_CONCEPTS keeps those identities and
CROSS_FORMAT_CONCEPT_IDS lists the readable ones; supports_concept and
concept_fallback (and their JavaScript counterparts) resolve a former identity
through current_concept_id.

fix: refresh formal-ai's self-AST census against the candidate crate

The census total_link_count grows by the grammar provenance link and the
hidden_text tokens split from grammar gap text (0daba06); named nodes, node
kinds and symbols are unchanged. The workload runs formal-ai's own
regenerate_self_ast_census example before its tests and fails when anything
but a total_link_count changes.

fix(js): bound the grammar parser's memory

- Grammars compile on first use instead of all 60 at import.
- Grammar modules compile with a tiering budget no parse exhausts: V8's
  background TurboFan tier-up of the 130-360 KB generated lexers (PowerShell,
  Swift, Markdown, Markdown inline) took 0.5-2 GB each and killed suites
  after their tests passed.
- String offsets map to UTF-8 bytes and points through typed-array
  checkpoints every 64 characters with a binary search.
- Markdown inline regions share one parser and still delete each tree.
chore: changelog for the parser memory and published concept fixes
fix(rust): satisfy clippy 1.99's assert_is_empty lint in the grammar union tests

ci(rust): gate compiling jobs on cargo check, split the test job by suite, cancel superseded PR runs

Every workflow now has a workflow-level concurrency group that cancels
superseded pull request runs. The Rust test job runs as four suites
(grammar, inference, translation, remaining) with 15-minute timeouts, and
the fresh-merge, MSRV, coverage and test jobs need a fast cargo check.

fix(js): read the strict merge policy with the workflow token

The required checks come from rules/branches/main, which the workflow token
can read. Only the bypass-actor list needs ISSUE_195_RULESET_TOKEN, and a
missing or rejected token fails only the non-bypassable assertion.
chore: register the d2407c18 audit as a requirement source

ci(js): run the issue #195 evidence as staged jobs the aggregate only merges

The single "Produce checkpoint evidence" step ran both runtime suites, the
runtime parity probe and every native toolchain in one process tree. The
evidence now runs as stages (javascript-suite, rust-suite, runtime-parity,
native-<target>, delivery, merge-enforcement), each a CI job that uploads
its record, logs and artifacts. The Full Requirements Aggregate downloads
the stage outputs, merges them and evaluates; a stage that fails or never
reports is one gate error naming it.

Local runs execute the stages one after another with a bounded build
environment (CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2, RUST_TEST_THREADS=2, CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0),
and each native stage deletes the compiler outputs no cell cites.

perf(parity): stream the Rust probe as NDJSON and keep entry digests, not full trees

The parity check read the Rust probe's ~100 MB observation from stdout with
a 512 MB maxBuffer and wrote both observations whole as artifacts. The probe
now writes one NDJSON record per section entry to a file, the check rebuilds
the observation record by record, sections are compared entry by entry, and
the kept evidence is digests.ndjson (one sha256 per entry and runtime),
differences.ndjson (both entries, only where they differ) and each runtime's
translations for the native stages.

feat(ledger): add atomic resource-limit rows for the CI split, agent rules and memory fixes

Registers the rows the resource audit (comment 5956284229) asks for, each
sourced to that comment and specified by the new docs/vision.md Resource
limits section: the compile gate, the test matrices, the evidence stages,
workflow concurrency, the AGENTS.md rules, the bounded sequential evidence
run, lazy grammars, the tiering budget, inline-parser reuse, source-boundary
checkpoints, parity digests, the cleanup wrapper and native output cleanup.
The tests that pin each behaviour now record its tooling cells, and a new
regression test pins Markdown inline-parser reuse.

fix(tests): keep parallel temporary directories apart and vision.md LF on Windows

The macOS grammar job failed linking a generated parser: two tests in one
process got the same microsecond timestamp, so one rustc removed the other's
.rcgu.o files. Temporary paths now carry a per-process sequence. The Windows
grammar job failed because docs/vision.md had CRLF endings and the feature
union test looks for a blank line. The runtime probe uses if let, as
clippy::single_match_else requires.

fix(js): keep a leading byte order mark when decoding UTF-8

TextDecoder strips a leading U+FEFF unless ignoreBOM is set, so a Links
Notation grammar with the literal %EF%BB%BF lost it on reading and the
text of a leaf at byte 0 dropped it.

feat(grammar): native merged JSON grammar checked against tree-sitter-json

parity/grammars/native/json.lino merges RFC 8259, ECMA-404 and
tree-sitter-json 0.24.8 and runs on both native executors. The fixture
parity/fixtures/native-grammars/json.json records the oracle rows the
native trees must equal, the RFC 8259 divergences and the invalid sources
the grammar rejects until it has recovery rules. Ledger row
I195-GRAMMAR-NATIVE-JSON tracks the JavaScript and Rust suites; CI runs
npm run check:native-grammars.
