## Path to a green PR and a release — every remaining requirement (audit of `6f727a4d`, 2026-10-03)

**The goal is a release, not a red gate.** This comment collects every requirement from issue #195, this PR's maintainer comments and the review sessions that is **not yet fully implemented**. It also fixes the CI design so that this PR can pass every check.

It **supersedes** every earlier statement, here or in the repository, that CI should stay red while work remains, including `AGENTS.md:34`: “A red aggregate while work remains is the truthful status”. This comment replaces the shorter correction previously posted here.

No capability requirement is reduced. Implementation is already authorized: do not ask for approval, scope decisions or credentials, and do not stop.

---

### 0. Maintainer decisions on CI and release (new, binding)

1. **Pull request CI checks only what exists before merge, and it must be able to pass.** Every PR check must turn green once the code in the PR is correct.
   - No PR check may depend on state that only exists after merge: published packages, live branch rules or rulesets, the status of the PR's own checks, the newest versions on live registries, or live edits of GitHub comments.
2. **CI on `main` does everything needed to produce the release.** It runs post-merge checks: published npm and crate verification, published-consumer runs for RML and formal-ai, merge-rule inspection, and live dependency freshness. If one of those fails after merge, we fix it in a follow-up commit. It must not block this PR.
3. **No tests for what comes after the pull request belong in the PR's required checks.**

#### Required CI changes

| Move out of PR checks (to `push` on `main`, `release` or `schedule`) | Where it is today |
| --- | --- |
| `I195-ACCEPTANCE-REQUIRED-MERGE-CHECK`. It can never pass: `failingCheckBlocksMerge` (`js/scripts/issue-195-merge-enforcement.mjs:152-157`) needs the aggregate that contains it to be **red** and the PR to be `BLOCKED`. Delete the `ISSUE_195_RULESET_TOKEN` dependency completely. If rule inspection stays at all, it runs on `main` as a non-blocking report. | `evidence-stages` matrix stage `merge-enforcement` in `issue-195-acceptance.yml` |
| `I195-DELIVERY-CRATE-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-NPM-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DELIVERY-RML-PUBLISHED`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-FORMAL-AI-PUBLISHED` (`release-delivery` checkpoint) | already on `release`; keep them **out of every PR check and out of the PR aggregate count** |
| `check-dependencies.mjs --delivery --live` (newest releases on live registries). A new upstream release turns the PR red without any code change. It caused the churn in `8ec42925` (libc), `3ccbc41d` (uuid), `ac6b3cc4` and `c3704dc1`. | `issue-195-acceptance.yml:142`, Clean Consumer job |
| `npm run check:issue-195:sources -- --online` (live comment hashes) | `js.yml:214` |
| `npm run check:documentation -- --online` (live links) | `js.yml:232` |

- **The merge rule already exists; there is nothing to unblock with credentials.** The live [ruleset 24204187](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/rules/24204187) is `enforcement: active` on `~DEFAULT_BRANCH`. It requires `Full Requirements Aggregate` with `strict_required_status_checks_policy: true`, and it has `current_user_can_bypass: never` and an empty bypass-actor list (read on 2026-10-02). No requirement asked for a bypass-actor proof or a new secret.
  - Any rule inspection kept on `main` uses only data the workflow token can read: `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/main`, plus the ruleset's `enforcement`, `conditions`, required checks, strict policy and `current_user_can_bypass`.
  - The “failing required check blocks merge” logic is unit-tested against **recorded snapshot fixtures**, with positive and negative cases, never against the live status of the aggregate that contains it.
- On the PR, dependency checks compare against the **committed** audit, offline. A scheduled workflow on `main` refreshes dependencies and opens its own PRs.
- Re-classify the moved rows to a `post-merge` checkpoint in `parity/issue-195-requirements.json`, citing this comment as the source. Re-classifying is a maintainer decision, not a weakened gate.
- **Add a gate self-test:** run the evaluator on a fixture in which every pre-merge row has passing evidence, and assert that the result is green. No row may require its own aggregate to fail.
- **Fix the release pipeline on `main`.** npm still serves only `meta-language@0.46.0` (2026-06-28). The latest `main` publish ([JavaScript workflow, 2026-08-20](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/workflows/js.yml?query=branch%3Amain)) fails with `npm error code ENEEDAUTH` under `auth mode 'oidc'`. Make the `main` release path publish the crate and the npm package from the merged commit. Document the exact npm trusted-publisher settings it expects in `docs/`.
- Update `AGENTS.md`, `docs/vision.md`, the PR body and the ledger text. Replace the red-by-design wording with: **“Every PR check must pass. A red check is a defect to fix now; unfinished requirements are work to implement, not a reason for red CI.”**

---

### 1. Where the PR stands

The Rust and JavaScript workflows are **green** at `6f727a4d`. Thanks for fixing the compile error, the JS↔Rust formal-ai regressions, the CI split and the parser memory. The only red check is **Full Requirements Aggregate**: [271/285 pre-merge rows pass](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/actions/runs/37093351458), and 14 fail:

| Area | Failing rows |
| --- | --- |
| Native grammars (section 2) | `I195-GRAMMAR-NATIVE-MERGED`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LANGUAGE-CATALOG`, `I195-GRAMMAR-LOSSLESS-TREES`, `I195-GRAMMAR-DEPENDENCY-BOUNDARY`, `I195-DEPENDENCY-PRODUCTION-PARSERS-REMOVED`, `I195-MERGE-AUTOMATIC-PIPELINE`, `I195-MERGE-SHIPPED-GRAMMARS-ARE-MERGED`, `I195-MERGE-QUALITY-EVIDENCE`, `I195-ACCEPTANCE-INDEPENDENT-ORACLES` |
| Grammar interchange (section 4) | `I195-INTERCHANGE-FORMAT-FEATURES`, `I195-INTERCHANGE-CROSS-FORMAT-TOOLS` |
| Semantics and downstream (section 4) | `I195-SEMANTICS-CONSTRUCT-INVENTORY`, `I195-DOWNSTREAM-TYPESCRIPT-TRANSLATIONS` |
| Post-merge (section 0) | `I195-ACCEPTANCE-REQUIRED-MERGE-CHECK` → **move out of PR checks** |

After section 0, **13 rows of real implementation work** decide whether this PR can merge. Nine of them are the native grammar work.

---

### 2. Main focus: real, complete native Links Notation grammars for every catalog language

**Status today:**

- 7 of the 70 non-natural-language catalog entries have a native grammar: JSON, INI, Diff, CSV, JSON5, Scheme and Racket.
- **None of the seven is the default parser.** [`docs/grammar/native-grammars.md` § Current limits](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/issue-195-cc10e17ab860/docs/grammar/native-grammars.md#current-limits) says that invalid input is rejected instead of recovered, so default parsing still uses tree-sitter. **Zero languages parse natively by default.**
- `web-tree-sitter` is a production npm dependency, and `rust/Cargo.toml` has 52 `tree-sitter` crates.

**Catalog entries that still need a native grammar.** The 10 natural languages need a stated, tested treatment of their own, not a tree-sitter grammar.

- **Programming (37):** JavaScript, TypeScript, TSX, Rust, Python, C, C++, C#, Java, Visual Basic, Delphi/Object Pascal, Go, R, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, Scala, Lua, Perl, Haskell, OCaml, OCaml Interface, Zig, Bash, Dart, Elixir, Elm, Erlang, Groovy, MATLAB, Nix, Odin, PowerShell, Solidity. Scheme and Racket are done, apart from recovery.
- **Formal (3):** Lean, Rocq, Agda.
- **Build (2):** CMake, Make.
- **Data (8):** HCL, YAML, TOML. Diff, JSON, INI, CSV and JSON5 are done, apart from recovery.
- **Pattern (1):** Regex.
- **SQL (8):** ANSI, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server, Oracle, BigQuery, Snowflake.
- **Markup, style and schema (6):** HTML, XML, CSS, DTD, Protocol Buffers, GraphQL.
- **Documents and meta (5):** Markdown, txt, PDF, DOCX, LiNo. State whether each is native already, and test it.

**What “done” means for each language.** Every point is required, in both runtimes, with identical output:

1. A native `.lino` grammar that is the **output of the automatic merge pipeline** over all of the language's pinned sources: the official specification, ANTLR grammars-v4, tree-sitter and other mature grammars. Scale by importing (the ANTLR and tree-sitter-JSON importers already exist) and merging, not by hand-copying. Hand edits are recorded as reviewed merge decisions. This covers `MERGE-AUTOMATIC-PIPELINE` and `MERGE-SHIPPED-GRAMMARS-ARE-MERGED`.
2. **Error recovery in the native executor**: error and missing nodes, plus synchronization. Implement it **once, in the executor**, so all seven existing grammars become default parsers immediately. Then every new grammar ships as the default parser. This covers `GRAMMAR-LOSSLESS-TREES` and `GRAMMAR-DEPENDENCY-BOUNDARY`.
3. **External scanners represented natively**: indentation and layout for Python, Haskell, Lean, Nix, Elm, YAML and Make; heredocs; raw strings; nested comments; template literals; context-sensitive lexing. This uses the feature-union constructs (lexical modes and state). No foreign scanner code may stay on the production path.
4. A lossless CST by default: kinds, fields, order, exact tokens and trivia, spans, error and missing nodes, embedded-language boundaries. An optional AST with provenance. The tree reloads without the source, can be edited, and is emitted and re-parsed.
5. Checked against **pinned independent oracles**, using several where available (tree-sitter, ANTLR, official compilers and provers), on upstream corpora **and real projects**. Every discrepancy is traced to a test with a justified resolution, as the existing native suites already do. This covers `ACCEPTANCE-INDEPENDENT-ORACLES` and `MERGE-QUALITY-EVIDENCE`, which also requires time and memory measurements.
6. Once a language parses natively by default, **move its tree-sitter grammar to dev or test dependencies only**. When the last one moves, `DEPENDENCY-PRODUCTION-PARSERS-REMOVED` passes.
7. The catalog lists versions, dialects, aliases, extensions and embedded languages, and pins every grammar source with its license and provenance. This covers `GRAMMAR-LANGUAGE-CATALOG`.

**Order of work** (to maximize reuse):

1. Executor recovery.
2. The four core languages: JavaScript with TypeScript and TSX, Rust, Lean and Rocq. Translation depends on them.
3. Family by family, so that shared concepts are designed once:
   - **C-family:** C, C++, C#, Java, Go, Kotlin, Scala, Swift, Dart, Groovy, Solidity, Zig, Odin, PHP.
   - **ML/functional:** OCaml, OCaml Interface, Haskell, Elm, Agda, Nix, Erlang, Elixir.
   - **Lisp:** finish Scheme and Racket with a shared base.
   - **Scripting:** Python, Ruby, Lua, Perl, R, Bash, PowerShell, MATLAB, Visual Basic, Pascal.
   - **SQL:** one shared base plus a delta for each dialect.
   - **Data and markup:** YAML, TOML, HCL, HTML, XML, DTD, CSS, GraphQL, Protocol Buffers, Regex, CMake, Make.

Commit and push **each language, or each small family, as soon as it passes its suites**. Partial progress is real progress as long as it is committed working code.

---

### 3. New requirement: the native grammars must use shared concepts

The meta-language library is real only if its grammars are written **in terms of shared concepts**. Then a construct that maps 1:1 in more than two languages is translated once, through its concept, instead of by a rule for every pair of languages.

**Today they are not.** For example, [`parity/grammars/native/json.lino`](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/blob/issue-195-cc10e17ab860/parity/grammars/native/json.lino) copies tree-sitter's node names (`_value`, `pair`, `object`) and has no reference to the concept records (`js/src/concept-records.js`, `parity/naming/canonical-concepts.json`). `json.lino`, `scheme.lino` and `racket.lino` contain no concept references at all. Scheme and Racket, and JSON and JSON5, were written independently, even though most of their constructs correspond 1:1.

**Required**, as new atomic ledger rows with JS and Rust tests:

- **Every rule of every native grammar maps to a canonical concept record.** It maps to a **shared** record when its meaning corresponds 1:1 in two or more languages, and to a language-specific record otherwise. Required distinctions stay intact (`I195-GRAMMAR-CONCEPT-DISTINCTIONS`): ordered vs unordered choice, integer and overflow models, binding rules, effects, universes. Concepts that look alike but differ are never merged.
- **Shared concept library.** Build it as the families above are merged, and add any concept that two or more grammars need. Examples:
  - literals: string, integer, floating-point, boolean, null;
  - identifier, line comment, block comment;
  - module, import, function definition, parameter list, call, block;
  - conditional, loop, assignment, binary and unary operation with an operator-precedence class;
  - class or record or structure, field;
  - list, array, map and object literals, key-value pair;
  - symbolic list (s-expression).
- **Tests:**
  1. A grammar test fails if any rule lacks a concept record.
  2. A per-language reuse report lists shared vs language-specific rules. It is published with `MERGE-QUALITY-EVIDENCE`.
  3. For every construct registered as 1:1 in three or more languages, an assertion checks that all of them resolve to **the same concept identity**. Examples: the JSON/JSON5 object and pair; Scheme/Racket list, symbol and boolean; function definition and call across JavaScript, TypeScript, Rust, Python and others.
  4. Negative fixtures prove that lookalike concepts stay distinct.
  5. A translation test proves that a construct shared by concept translates between two languages **with no pairwise rule**.
- **Names:**
  - Concept and rule names follow the readable-English naming rule: unabbreviated noun phrases for concepts, verb phrases for operations. `_value` and similar inherited names become English names; the original tree-sitter and ANTLR names are kept as aliases for reverse conversion.
  - Extend `npm run check:naming` to cover native grammar rule names and concept references.

---

### 4. The other open implementation rows

- **`I195-INTERCHANGE-FORMAT-FEATURES`:** every feature of BNF, EBNF, ABNF, PEG, Peggy, Pest, ANTLR, tree-sitter source and JSON, Lark, GBNF, Yacc/Bison and lexer specifications gets an explicit native representation and operational meaning. Imports follow included grammars, lexer and scanner definitions and actions, and keep comments, locations, original names and formatting provenance.
- **`I195-INTERCHANGE-CROSS-FORMAT-TOOLS`:** cross-format conversions, and native → external → native cycles, run under the **actual independent target tools**. They compare accepted and rejected programs, structure, lexical decisions, precedence, actions and diagnostics. The target tools are pinned dev dependencies installed in CI, not on the agent's machine.
- **`I195-SEMANTICS-CONSTRUCT-INVENTORY`:** JavaScript, Rust, Lean and Rocq. Cover classes and objects, arrays and mutation, standard-library behavior, imports, higher-order functions, async, ownership, macros and notation, types, universes, effects, proofs and tactics. Each must be represented and transformed through the common links, and normal JavaScript must be accepted without annotations. This builds on the core-language native grammars in section 2.
- **`I195-DOWNSTREAM-TYPESCRIPT-TRANSLATIONS`:** both runtimes translate the required Rust/JavaScript/TypeScript projection pairs from formal-ai's own fixtures and rules, using clean installed candidate artifacts (pre-merge candidates, not published packages). A TypeScript CST alone does not count.

---

### 5. Other requirements from the conversation, and their state

| Requirement (source) | State |
| --- | --- |
| Full representation and transformation of JavaScript, Rust, Rocq and Lean; **all existing languages as CST by default** ([clarification](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5795832509)) | CSTs exist, but **through tree-sitter**. Native default parsing is section 2. |
| No limitations: meta-language represents every concept of every popular language and grammar; shared concepts reused ([directive](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5885245090)) | **Not yet**: section 3. |
| Test against the top existing grammars (ANTLR, tree-sitter and others) and **reimplement them in Links Notation instead of importing them** | Section 2: seven partial grammars so far. |
| Tools to import, convert, automatically merge and **convert back** grammars in every popular format, with round-trip tests | Import, export, merge, renaming and reverse conversion pass. Open: section 4 rows. **The pipeline does not yet produce the shipped grammars** (section 2, point 1). |
| Automatic recognition of duplicate concepts with different names; fully automatic merging; renaming | The rows pass on fixtures. They must now run on **real multi-source merges for every language**. |
| English noun and verb phrases with no abbreviations, with tests | The check exists. **Extend it to native grammar rules** (section 3). |
| Update all dependencies, including Links Notation | Done for this PR; 28 retained items are behind and recorded. Ongoing freshness → scheduled job on `main` (section 0). |
| Vision recorded in the repository, and contradictions fixed repository-wide | `docs/vision.md` exists. **`AGENTS.md:34` contradicts the new CI decision**: fix it (section 0). |
| RML and formal-ai needs covered | Pinned workloads pass on candidates. Open: TypeScript translations. Published-consumer checks → `main` (section 0). |
| Clean build caches on commit and other events; bounded resources | Done (`clean-caches.mjs`, `with-cache-cleanup.mjs`, parser memory fixes, NDJSON parity). Keep it, and see section 6. |
| Everything delivered in **this single PR**, with no scope split | Still in force. |

---

### 6. Reminder for the next AI agent: protect resources or you will be killed

Earlier sessions on this PR were **killed with exit code 137 (out of memory)**, and others stopped at the auto-restart limit. All of the work below is long, so:

- **Work in batches.** Write a whole language or family (grammar, tests, ledger row), commit, re-read the diff, then **push**. CI is the full verifier. Commit early and often, so a kill loses nothing.
- **Experiment in JavaScript first**, which needs no compile step. Port to Rust in one batch, then run a single `cargo check`.
- **Run only targeted local checks:** the one native-grammar suite you touched (`node --test tests/issue-195-grammar-native-<language>.test.js`, `cargo test --test unit issue_195_grammar_native_<language>`), with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=2 RUST_TEST_THREADS=2 CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0`. Wrap them in `node scripts/with-cache-cleanup.mjs`.
- **Never run locally:** the full acceptance pipeline, `run-issue-195-evidence.mjs`, the native Lean, Rocq and Rust toolchain matrix, clean-consumer installs, the RML and formal-ai workloads, `cargo llvm-cov`, or whole-corpus and whole-registry experiments.
- **Load only the grammars you need.** Process large corpora file by file (streaming), never all at once. Check memory (`free -m`) before any heavy step.
- **Always be ready to clean up.** Run `node scripts/clean-caches.mjs` after each batch. Delete `.issue-195-work/`, `issue-195-results/`, `issue-195-artifacts/` and temporary clones. After any timeout, kill leftover `cargo`, `rustc`, `node`, `lean`, `lake`, `coqc` and `rocq` processes.
- **Do not wait on CI in a loop.** Push, then continue with the next language while CI runs. Come back to fix any red check before you finish the session.

---

### Completion condition

Every PR check is green, and the PR is mergeable. All 13 implementation rows and the new shared-concept rows pass. Every catalog language parses **natively by default** through merged, concept-based Links Notation grammars in both runtimes, with tree-sitter and ANTLR kept only as test oracles. After merge, CI on `main` publishes the npm package and the crate and runs the post-merge checks.

Register **this comment** in `parity/issue-195-sources.json` and reconcile the ledger: add the new rows, re-classify the post-merge rows and update `AGENTS.md`.

## 🔄 Auto-restart 1/5

**Reason:** New comment(s) from non-bot user(s): konard

Starting new session to address the issues.

---
*Auto-restart-until-mergeable mode is active. This run will stop after 5 restart iterations in total.*

message:
ci(issue-195): pull request checks depend only on pre-merge state

Move the live merge-enforcement inspection to a post-merge checkpoint that
runs on main as a non-blocking report with the workflow token, and delete
the ISSUE_195_RULESET_TOKEN dependency. Pull requests compare dependencies
offline against the committed audit; --live, --online source and
documentation comparisons run only on main. Add a scheduled dependency
refresh on main and a gate self-test row asserting the pre-merge aggregate
is green when every pre-merge row passes.

Addresses https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5965533606 (section 0).

ci(issue-195): clean regenerable caches after the post-merge report

The cache policy requires every job that runs npm or cargo to end with
the ci-teardown cleanup step.

ci(release): publish npm from the release tag and verify the trusted-publisher exchange

The npm publish job failed with ENEEDAUTH in OIDC mode: npm treats a
refused trusted-publisher exchange as "no credential" and hides the
registry's answer. The job now performs the same exchange first and
reports the registry response, the matched OIDC claims and the exact
settings. rust.yml dispatches js.yml on the release tag, so npm gets the
merged commit the crate came from. docs/ci-cd/npm-trusted-publishing.md
documents the exact npmjs.com settings (link-foundation / meta-language /
js.yml / no environment).

Addresses https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5965533606 (section 0, release pipeline).

feat(grammar): automatic error recovery in the JavaScript native executor

errorRecovery repairs a failed parse without recovery rules: at the farthest
failing element a zero-width MISSING leaf or a skip to the element's next
match behind an ERROR leaf, chosen by least repair cost, in rounds of repair
points bounded by maxRepairs. Every rejection of the seven native grammar
fixtures records its lossless recovered tree (I195-GRAMMAR-NATIVE-RECOVERY).

feat(grammar): automatic error recovery in the Rust native executor

Ports the JavaScript repair rounds to rust/src/grammar/feature_runtime:
FeatureParseOptions gains error_recovery and max_repairs, results carry a
repair cost, and a failed parse is repaired into ERROR and MISSING leaves.
rust/tests/unit/issue_195_grammar_native_recovery.rs checks that every
recorded rejection of parity/fixtures/native-grammars/*.json is repaired
into the tree the JavaScript executor recorded.

perf(grammar): linear-time joins in both native executors

Joining results copied every child before the join, so a repetition of n
items cost O(n²) time and memory and a 737 KB JSON document ran out of
memory. A join now links its two parts with their child count; the list is
flattened once when first read, and rule nodes share the unflattened list.
A 10,000-item repetition repaired near its end is tested in JS and Rust.

issue.title: fix: report OOM recovery truthfully — one completion per exit, ⚠️ recovered status, total time, in-process resume after SIGKILL (#2408)

repository.name: hive-mind
repository.description: The AI that controls AIs to do the automation of automation.

issue.body:
Fixes #2408

## What happened

The `/claude https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196 --think high` task ran for about 17 hours and hit two out-of-memory events:

- **22:47.** `npm run check` was OOM-killed (exit 137). Claude **survived** and carried on. Docker set the container-wide `State.OOMKilled` flag, which stays set until the container exits.
- **07:08.** solve stopped **on purpose** ("Auto-restart limit reached after 5 iterations"), and the container exited 1. Because the sticky flag was still set, the bot read this as an OOM casualty. It spent its whole recovery budget (1/1) on a fresh launch with a new execution id, and the log was split.
- **07:11.** Three overlapping monitor ticks completed the old session three times. The last one overwrote "recovering" with **"❌ Work session failed (exit code: 1)"**, while `/queue` showed the recovery as processing for 5h 31m.
- **13:37.** Two Claude subagents ran `cargo test` in separate worktrees, and the kernel SIGKILLed Claude (exit 137). solve stopped and posted two failure reports, and the container exited 1. Six overlapping monitor ticks then posted six logs and six notices. One of them contained `[object Object]`.

The timeline, evidence (sanitized log excerpts, PR comment data, the issue screenshots) and research are in [`docs/case-studies/issue-2408/README.md`](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2408-251fa28f0ba5/docs/case-studies/issue-2408/README.md).

## Root causes and fixes

| #   | Problem | Fix | Test (`tests/issue-2408-oom-recovery-reporting.test.mjs`) |
| --- | ------- | --- | ---- |
| RC1 | The 30 s `setInterval` monitor overlapped itself while a completion uploaded a 100 MB log, so one exit was completed 3× and 6×. Later copies found the budget spent and reported ❌ | `sessionsInFlight` per-session guard in `monitorSessions`; `already-recovered` latch in `recoverKilledSession` | "overlapping monitor ticks recover a killed session once and report it once", "a repeated completion for an already-recovered session does not start another one" |
| RC2 | Exit 1 + sticky `OOMKilled` read before the log footer was classified as "killed: out of memory" | Only exit 137 (or no exit code) with a dead backend is a kill; exit 1–127 is an OOM *event* during a failed session | "an exit 1 with the OOM flag and no footer yet is a survived OOM event, not a kill" |
| RC3 | A deliberate solve stop after a survived OOM event spent the recovery budget | New `session-kill-attribution.lib.mjs` scans the log tail for solve's own stop markers (auto-restart, auto-resume or usage limit). The exit is reported, not recovered | "a deliberate solve stop after an OOM event is reported, not recovered" |
| RC4 | A budget of 1 cannot cover a second OOM in a long run | `--session-kill-resume-attempts` defaults to 3 (docs in 4 languages) | "a second OOM in a long run can still be recovered by default" |
| RC5 | A SIGKILLed AI tool (exit 137) ended the whole `--auto-restart-until-mergeable` / watch run | New `solve.tool-kill-resume.lib.mjs` posts "⚠️ Working process killed (exit code 137, likely out of memory)" and resumes the **same** session in the same container and log. The feedback asks Claude to run builds one at a time. It shares the budget above | "a tool process killed by SIGKILL resumes its own session in-process, with a warning" |
| RC6 | Kill notice printed `[object Object]` as the manual resume command | Render `command.display` | "the pull-request notice renders a resume command object, never \"[object Object]\"" |
| RC7 | Task message and `/queue` showed only the recovery session's time, with no notion of "recovered" | `rootStartTime` + recovery count. The headline is ⚠️ "Work session finished successfully after automatic recovery (automatic recoveries: N)". `/queue` shows the total time and `🔁 N` (new `recovered`/`recoveries` keys in en/ru/hi/zh) | "the headline says how many automatic recoveries the work needed", "the queue shows the total active time of recovered work and its recovery count" |
| RC8 | Log split across execution ids: a resource-limited session cannot use start-command's same-container resume, because `docker commit` + `docker run` drops the limits | On start-command ≥ 0.35.0 (start#176, now pinned) a resource-limited session **resumes in place** under the same id and log. The `$` version gates it, CPU/RAM are re-asserted with `docker update`, and the writable-layer usage so far is carried into the disk allowance (`containerFilesystemInheritedBytes`). With an older `$`, the message names the earlier logs, for example `🆔 Execution: 88951cec (earlier logs: 0760afb4)` (`previousExecutionUuids` is persisted). Upstream: link-foundation/start#176 | "a fresh recovery launch keeps pointing at the earlier execution logs"; `tests/test-issue-2408-limited-in-place-resume.mjs` |
| RC9 | "…backend is still alive" verbose line printed on every poll (10,047 lines in one bot log) | Printed once per session | "the still-alive OOM verbose line is printed once, not on every poll" |
| RC10 | Two failure reports from one solve run (5953703216 + 5953753740) | Already fixed in v2.33.5 (#2397); the incident ran on 2.33.2 | "the exit notifier does not post a second failure report after the loop posted one" |

The citation for the sticky `State.OOMKilled` semantics now points at moby's `daemon/monitor.go` (`EventOOM`) and `daemon/container/state.go` (`SetRunning`).

## Follow-up: the 2026-10-03 rerun (PR comment)

The rerun of the same task (solve v2.33.7, bot still on pre-PR code) repeated RC3 and RC1 between [5965062164](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5965062164) and [5965532446](https://github.com/link-foundation/meta-language/pull/196#issuecomment-5965532446). solve stopped on purpose ("❌ Auto-restart 5/5 - limit reached", exit 1), but an OOM event at 16:55 the day before had left the sticky `OOMKilled` flag set. The bot therefore started recovery session `9187bb95`, which runs `solve` again with a fresh auto-restart budget: this is why it "continued to work in the background". Three more overlapping ticks posted three more log + notice pairs, and the last one set Telegram to ❌.

- **Regression test** on the real log tail (`docs/case-studies/issue-2408/logs/solve-log-7edfe0cf-auto-restart-limit-tail.txt`): four concurrent ticks → no launch, one notice, one Telegram completion, and one `session_kill_recovery_decision` event with `deliberateStop=auto-restart-limit`, `attemptRecovery=false`.
- **Every restart path audited** (solve auto-restart, auto-resume, in-process tool-kill resume, bot kill/OOM recovery, start-command `--on-kill-resume`); the triggers and bounds are in the [case study](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2408-251fa28f0ba5/docs/case-studies/issue-2408/README.md#audit-of-every-restart-path).
- **Gaps found by the audit and fixed**, each with a test in `tests/issue-2408-restart-paths.test.mjs` that fails before the fix:
  - B1: a session SIGKILLed *after* solve printed "❌ Auto-restart limit reached" was still recovered. The deliberate-stop check now covers killed sessions too.
  - B2: exit 0 + sticky flag + no footer yet was turned into "oom-killed" (137). A terminal exit 0 now stays a success.
  - B3: "No progress between sessions" / "identical results" and "SUBSCRIPTION/ACCESS UNAVAILABLE" are now deliberate stops. "AI session failed" stays recoverable (#2301).
  - B4: `/stop <root id>`, the id the chat shows, did not reach the recovery session, so a user stop was followed by another automatic recovery. It now matches `executionUuid`, `rootSessionName` and `killRecoveryOfSession`.
  - B5: a resumed solve child killed by a signal made the auto-continue parent `process.exit(null)`, i.e. **0**. It now exits 128 + n (SIGKILL → 137) and logs the signal.
  - B7: stop markers matched anywhere in a line, including quoted tool output. They are now anchored to the start of a log line.
- **Logging:** `session_kill_recovery_decision` (exit code, status, killed, oomEventOnly, deliberateStop, diskLimitExceeded, attemptRecovery) for every kill/OOM exit; `session_kill_not_recovered` with the reason; `[VERBOSE]` lines for the skipped recovery and for the `$` version gate.
- **Upstream:** start-command 0.35.0's new `--on-kill-resume` has the same sticky-flag bug, one layer down (`isKilledExit(1, "true") === true`), so it is not used. Filed as [link-foundation/start#178](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/178) with a repro and fix.
- **Dependencies:** start-command 0.35.0 (Dockerfile, Dockerfile.dind, Dockerfile.e2e), eslint 10.12.0 and secretlint 13.0.7. `npm outdated` is now empty, `@link-assistant/agent` 0.26.11 is the latest, and every GitHub Action is at its latest release.

## Answers to the questions in the issue

- **Does `0760afb4` contain the full 15 hours?** No. It covers 20:38:25 → 07:09:43 (10h 31m). The recovery ran as a fresh launch with execution `88951cec` and its own log. With start-command ≥ 0.35.0 (pinned here) a resource-limited recovery now stays in the same id and log. With an older `$`, the Telegram message names both ids.
- **The "crazy comments" after 5953703216:** see [The thirteen comments](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/blob/issue-2408-251fa28f0ba5/docs/case-studies/issue-2408/README.md#the-thirteen-comments-after-5953703216). Each one maps to RC1–RC6 or RC10.
- **start-command initial + recovery command:** filed as [link-foundation/start#176](https://github.com/link-foundation/start/issues/176), with a repro, workaround and suggested fix. The repro is `experiments/issue-2408-docker-commit-drops-limits.sh`: the original container has `Memory=268435456 … PidsLimit=64`, and the resumed one has `Memory=0 … PidsLimit=<no value>`.

## How to reproduce / verify

```bash
node tests/issue-2408-oom-recovery-reporting.test.mjs   # 13/13 pass
node tests/test-issue-2408-limited-in-place-resume.mjs  # 27/27 pass
node --test tests/issue-2408-restart-paths.test.mjs     # 5/5 pass (all 5 fail on the code before the fix)
node experiments/issue-2408-start-command-version-probe.mjs  # prints the installed `$` version and the in-place gate
```

On `main` (with only the two new modules copied in so that the imports resolve), 10 of the 12 tests fail. The two that pass are the tool-kill test, whose module comes from this PR, and the duplicate-report test, which was already fixed by #2397. The existing OOM and kill suites (#2134, #2301) were updated for the new default budget and pass.

## Unrelated CI fixes

`@sentry/node` and `@sentry/profiling-node` 11.3.0 and 11.4.0 were published on 2026-10-02 (12:56 and 16:37 UTC). After each release, the dependency-freshness gate failed on every branch, so the pins are refreshed to `^11.4.0`, following ef33600b. The #2187 pin test follows the new pins.

The Broken Link Checker failed on `main` (08:24 and 12:14 UTC) and on branches on 2026-10-02. Every error was a `503` from github.com, and every one was for one of the seven `github.com/.../blob/...` URLs that lychee checks here. These URLs answer 200 outside Actions. This branch first fixed it with a lychee `--remap` of blob URLs to `raw.githubusercontent.com` (a677ca60, Check Links green). `main` then merged #2423, which re-checks transient failures with backoff and checks blob pages through the contents API. After merging `main`, this PR drops the remap so only `main`’s mechanism remains, and it does not change the link workflow. The evidence and the remap, kept as a token-free alternative, are in `experiments/issue-2408-link-check-503/`.

## Remaining limits

- A recovered resource-limited session still has two log files when the installed `$` is older than 0.35.0.
- A genuine OOM recovery runs `solve --resume` as a new solve process, so solve's auto-restart counter starts again. The total is bounded by `--session-kill-resume-attempts` (default 3).
- A real cgroup OOM cannot be reproduced end to end in this sandbox (no memory cgroup controller); the tests replay real log tails and statuses.
- The in-process resume (RC5) works only when solve itself survives the OOM kill. Otherwise the bot-level recovery (RC1–RC4) handles it.
- The raw bot logs and the 46 MB solve log of `0760afb4` (from a private repository) were analysed but not committed. Only sanitized excerpts are in the case study.
